76828.q: What has happened here in the football match?
76828.e: The ball flies into the goal, and everyone cheers. That is a goal.
76828.m: When the ball is completely in the goal, the goal counts.

76829.q: Who shows these cards in football?
76829.e: The referee shows the yellow and red cards. That is how he punishes fouls.
76829.m: The referee shows the yellow card and the red card.

76830.q: Which big tournament do these pictures show?
76830.e: Trophy, football and globe mean: the best teams in the world play for the trophy. That is the football World Cup.
76830.m: At the World Cup, teams from all over the world play.

76831.q: Who is at the football with a scarf and a loud voice?
76831.e: With a scarf and a megaphone, you cheer on your team. That is what fans do.
76831.m: Fans cheer on their team in the stadium.

76832.q: Which footballer is allowed to do what these pictures show?
76832.e: Gloves and a hand on the ball: only the goalkeeper may catch the ball with his hands in his penalty area.
76832.m: Only the goalkeeper may catch the ball with his hands in the penalty area.

76833.q: How many players of a football team are on the pitch if you add these numbers together?
76833.e: 10 plus 1 makes 11. A football team has 11 players on the pitch.
76833.m: A football team plays with 11 players.

76834.q: What is football played on in this stadium?
76834.e: The little green plant stands for grass. Football is usually played on grass.
76834.m: Football is usually played on green grass.

76835.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76835.e: Football and boot together make football boot. It has studs so that you do not slip on the grass.
76835.m: Football boots have studs on the sole.

76836.q: What pulls the skiers up the slope on this hook?
76836.e: Skis, an arrow pointing up and a hook show the ski lift. It pulls the skiers up by the bar.
76836.m: The ski lift pulls the skiers up the slope.

76837.q: What do the skiers sit on here to go up the mountain?
76837.e: A chair, an arrow pointing up and skis: on a chairlift you sit and go up.
76837.m: On a chairlift you go up the mountain sitting down.

76838.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76838.e: Ski and boot together make ski boot. The ski boot clicks firmly onto the ski.
76838.m: The ski boot holds your foot firmly on the ski.

76839.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76839.e: Ski and helmet together make ski helmet. It protects your head when you ski.
76839.m: A ski helmet protects your head on the slopes.

76840.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76840.e: Goggles, snow and skis make ski goggles. They protect your eyes from wind and snow.
76840.m: Ski goggles protect your eyes from wind and snow.

76841.q: Which competition is meant by these pictures?
76841.e: Skis, stopwatch and medal: whoever gets down the slope fastest wins the ski race.
76841.m: In a ski race, the fastest person wins.

76842.q: Which vehicle makes the ski slope smooth again at night?
76842.e: Moon, vehicle and skis: at night, the snow groomer drives over the slope on its wide tracks and makes the snow smooth again.
76842.m: The snow groomer makes the ski slope smooth at night.

76843.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76843.e: Ski and school building together make ski school. That is where children learn to ski.
76843.m: You learn to ski at ski school.

76844.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76844.e: Swimming and pool together make swimming pool.
76844.m: At the swimming pool you can swim and bathe.

76845.q: What do you do with this mask among the fish?
76845.e: With a diving mask and snorkel, you look at the fish underwater. That is diving.
76845.m: When you dive, you look underwater.

76846.q: What do these pictures show together?
76846.e: Swimmer, stopwatch and medal: whoever swims fastest wins the swimming competition.
76846.m: In a swimming competition, the fastest swimmer wins.

76847.q: Which swimming stroke is meant by these pictures?
76847.e: In breaststroke you move your legs like a frog. That is why the picture shows a frog.
76847.m: In breaststroke you kick with your legs like a frog.

76848.q: What do you put on your feet to swim faster like a fish?
76848.e: Feet, a fish and a swimmer: with flippers on your feet, you swim faster, almost like a fish.

76849.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
76849.e: A teacher is teaching a child to swim. That is a swimming teacher.
76849.m: The swimming teacher teaches children to swim.

76850.q: What do you slide down into the water at the swimming pool?
76850.e: The swirl stands for a slide that goes round in circles, plus water and fun. You whizz down the water slide into the pool.
76850.m: You whizz down the water slide into the water.

76851.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76851.e: Water and ball together make the ball for water polo. Water polo is played in the swimming pool.
76851.m: Water polo is played swimming in the water.

76852.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76852.e: Bike and helmet together make bike helmet. It protects your head when you ride a bike.
76852.m: A bike helmet protects your head when cycling.

76853.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76853.e: Bike and bell together make bike bell. You use it to warn other people.
76853.m: You warn other people with your bike bell.

76854.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76854.e: Bike and lock together make bike lock. You use it to lock up your bike.
76854.m: A bike lock protects your bike from thieves.

76855.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76855.e: Bike and light bulb together make bike light. In the dark, the light must be on.
76855.m: In the dark, a bike needs a light.

76856.q: What do you have to do on your bike when the traffic light looks like this?
76856.e: The traffic light is red. On red, you have to stop your bike.

76857.q: Which bike goes with these pictures?
76857.e: Bike, mountain and forest show a bike for steep paths in rough country. That is a mountain bike.
76857.m: You ride a mountain bike on mountain paths.

76858.q: Which bike is meant by these pictures?
76858.e: Two people are riding on one single bike. That is a tandem.
76858.m: On a tandem, two people ride together.

76859.q: Which competition is meant by these pictures?
76859.e: Bike, stopwatch and trophy: whoever rides fastest wins the cycle race.
76859.m: In a cycle race, whoever rides fastest wins.

76860.q: Which vehicle is meant by these pictures?
76860.e: The number 3 and a bike for small children: that is a tricycle with three wheels.

76861.q: What do you paint on the smooth stone here?
76861.e: Stone, brush and ladybird: you paint a smooth stone red and put black spots on it.
76861.m: You can paint a smooth stone to look like a ladybird.

76862.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76862.e: Paper and boat together make paper boat.
76862.m: You fold a paper boat out of paper.

76863.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76863.e: Chestnut and man together make a chestnut figure, or conker man. You make it in autumn with cocktail sticks.
76863.m: In autumn, people make little figures out of chestnuts.

76864.q: What do you stick on the paper here for an autumn picture?
76864.e: Autumn leaves, a picture and scissors show it: you cut colourful leaves to shape and stick them on to make an autumn picture.
76864.m: You can make a picture by sticking on colourful autumn leaves.

76865.q: What do you make for the procession in November?
76865.e: A lantern, a candle and a walking person show the lantern procession. For it, you make a lantern with a light inside.
76865.m: For the lantern procession, you make a lantern.

76866.q: What do you do with these things?
76866.e: With thread and a needle, you sew fabric together.
76866.m: To sew, you need a needle and thread.

76867.q: What do you do to turn this wool into a scarf?
76867.e: You knit a scarf from a ball of wool with needles.
76867.m: You can knit a scarf from wool.

76868.q: What are you making here for Fasnacht, the Swiss carnival?
76868.e: The theatre face and the scissors show it: you cut out a mask. At Fasnacht, people wear masks.
76868.m: At Fasnacht, lots of people wear masks.

76869.q: Which colour do you get when you mix these two colours?
76869.e: Red and yellow mixed make orange.
76869.m: Red and yellow together make orange.

76870.q: Which colour do you get when you mix these two colours?
76870.e: Blue and yellow mixed make green.
76870.m: Blue and yellow together make green.

76871.q: Which colour do you get when you mix these two colours?
76871.e: Red and blue mixed make purple.
76871.m: Red and blue together make purple.

76872.q: Which colour do you get when you mix these two colours?
76872.e: White and black mixed make grey.
76872.m: White and black together make grey.

76873.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
76873.e: An artist who paints pictures needs a brush, a canvas and a palette.
76873.m: An artist paints pictures with a brush and paint.

76874.q: What do you paint with here instead of a brush?
76874.e: A finger and a palette: in finger painting, you dip your fingers straight into the paint.
76874.m: In finger painting, you paint with your fingers.

76875.q: What is being painted with the brush here?
76875.e: A child is getting a tiger face with a brush. Here a face is being painted.
76875.m: In face painting, you paint on someone’s face.

76876.q: Who is this child painting while looking in the mirror?
76876.e: In the mirror, the child sees themselves. So the child paints a picture of themselves, a self-portrait.

76877.q: Which instrument is meant by these pictures?
76877.e: The picture shows a string instrument that you tuck under your chin and play with a bow. That is a violin.
76877.m: You play a violin with a bow.

76878.q: Which wind instrument do these pictures show?
76878.e: The picture shows a curved, golden wind instrument with lots of keys. That is a saxophone.
76878.m: The saxophone is a wind instrument with lots of keys.

76879.q: What do you write on the lines here so that you can play a song?
76879.e: A stave and a pencil show it: you write down notes. They show which sounds you play.
76879.m: You write music down with notes.

76880.q: What do you call a group that sings together?
76880.e: Lots of speaking heads and notes show it: lots of people are singing together. That is a choir.
76880.m: In a choir, lots of people sing together.

76881.q: What do you call a big group that plays lots of instruments together?
76881.e: Violin, trumpet, drum and piano: when lots of musicians play together, that is an orchestra.
76881.m: In an orchestra, lots of musicians play together.

76882.e: With the microphone and the notes, the girl is singing a song.
76882.m: When you sing, you use your own voice.

76883.q: What do you do to this music?
76883.e: The woman is moving to the music. She is dancing.

76884.q: Where is the music coming from here?
76884.e: The device with an aerial and a loudspeaker is a radio. Music and news come out of it.
76884.m: You hear music and news on the radio.

76885.q: What do you put in a book so that you can find the page again?
76885.e: The open book and the ribbon show a bookmark. It shows where you stopped reading.
76885.m: A bookmark shows where you can carry on reading.

76886.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
76886.e: Book, writing hand and woman: a writer writes books.

76887.q: Which story is meant by these pictures?
76887.e: Moon, book and a tired face: before you fall asleep, you listen to a bedtime story.
76887.m: People often read a bedtime story before going to sleep.

76888.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76888.e: The frying pan stands for cooking. Cooking and book together make cookbook. It has recipes in it.
76888.m: A cookbook has recipes in it.

76889.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76889.e: A musical note and a book together make songbook. It has songs in it for singing.
76889.m: A songbook has songs in it.

76890.q: Which book is meant by these pictures?
76890.e: Picture, book and a small child: a picture book has lots of pictures and little text.
76890.m: A picture book has lots of colourful pictures.

76891.q: Which kind of book has speech bubbles like these?
76891.e: Speech bubbles and pictures in boxes belong to a comic.
76891.m: In a comic, the characters speak in speech bubbles.

76892.q: Which book is meant by these pictures?
76892.e: Map and book: an atlas is a book full of maps.
76892.m: You find lots of maps in an atlas.

76893.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76893.e: The book stands for reading. Reading and glasses together make reading glasses. With them, you see the letters more clearly.
76893.m: With reading glasses you see small letters better.

76894.q: Which shoes do you need for this outing?
76894.e: A person is going up a mountain. For that you need sturdy hiking boots.
76894.m: For mountain paths you need sturdy hiking boots.

76895.q: What helps hikers find the right way?
76895.e: The compass shows the direction, and you can see the paths on the map. That is how you find the right way.
76895.m: With a compass and a map you can find your way.

76896.q: What is this sign with an arrow for hikers called?
76896.e: A sign with an arrow shows hikers the direction. That is a signpost. In Switzerland, hiking signposts are usually yellow.
76896.m: The signpost shows hikers the way.

76897.q: Which alpine flower do these pictures make together?
76897.e: The gem stands for ‘edel’, German for noble, and the circle for ‘weiss’, white. Together they make Edelweiss.
76897.m: The edelweiss is a well-known flower of the Alps.

76898.e: A mountain and the word TOP: the hiker is right at the top, on the summit.
76898.m: The summit is the highest point of a mountain.

76899.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76899.e: Water falls downwards. Water and fall together make waterfall.
76899.m: At a waterfall, water plunges down into the depths.

76900.q: Which alpine flower do these pictures make together?
76900.e: Alps and rose together make alpine rose. It flowers pinkish-red in the mountains.
76900.m: The alpine rose flowers in the mountains in summer.

76901.q: What does the cow wear around its neck on the alpine pasture?
76901.e: Cow, bell and mountains: on the alp, lots of cows wear a bell. That way you can hear where they are.
76901.m: On the alp, lots of cows wear a bell.

76902.q: Which animal do these pictures make together?
76902.e: Snow and hare together make snow hare. It lives in the Alps and has white fur in winter.
76902.m: The snow hare has white fur in winter.

76903.q: What is this girl doing on the hill?
76903.e: The girl is riding down the hill on a sledge. She is sledging.
76903.m: When you go sledging, you sit on the sledge.

76904.q: What kind of board is this person riding down the slope on?
76904.e: A mountain and a snowboarder show it: you stand with both feet on a wide board in the snow. That is a snowboard.
76904.m: On a snowboard, both feet stand on one board.

76905.q: What do you put on to go sledging in this weather?
76905.e: Snow and a freezing face show the cold. So you put on a warm winter jacket.
76905.m: In winter, a warm jacket keeps your body warm.

76906.q: Which bird likes to slide on its tummy over snow and ice?
76906.e: Penguin, ice and snow: penguins cannot fly. They often slide on their tummies over ice and snow.
76906.m: Penguins like to slide on their tummies.

76907.q: Which winter sport do these pictures show?
76907.e: A stone, ice and a broom belong to curling. You push the stone across the ice.
76907.m: In curling, a stone glides across the ice.

76908.q: What are these children doing in the snow?
76908.e: Two children are throwing snow at each other. That is a snowball fight.
76908.m: In a snowball fight, you throw snowballs.

76909.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
76909.e: A stick with a puck and ice belong to ice hockey.
76909.m: Ice hockey is played with a stick and a puck.

76910.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76910.e: Snow and angel together make snow angel. You lie down in the snow and move your arms and legs.
76910.m: You make a snow angel by lying down in the snow.

76911.q: Which circus character do these pictures show?
76911.e: Red nose, funny face: that is the clown, who makes everyone laugh.
76911.m: At the circus, the clown makes everyone laugh.

76912.q: Which circus character do these pictures show?
76912.e: The person throws several balls into the air and catches them again. That is a juggler.
76912.m: A juggler throws balls into the air.

76913.q: Who pulls this rabbit out of the hat at the circus?
76913.e: A rabbit out of a top hat is a famous magic trick.
76913.m: A magician pulls a rabbit out of the hat.

76914.q: Who walks high up on this thing at the circus?
76914.e: A person walks high up across a rope. That is a tightrope walker.
76914.m: The tightrope walker balances on a rope.

76915.q: Which circus performers do these pictures show?
76915.e: The person does a cartwheel and jumps. That is what acrobats do.

76916.q: Which animals are running in a circle in the ring here?
76916.e: The picture shows a horse running in a circle in the round circus ring.
76916.m: At the circus, horses often run in the round ring.

76917.q: What does the audience do when they have enjoyed the show?
76917.e: Circus tent and clapping hands: at the end, the audience gives loud applause.
76917.m: If they like it, the audience claps.

76918.q: What is the performer riding here?
76918.e: The number 1 and a bike show a vehicle with only one wheel. That is a unicycle.
76918.m: A unicycle has only one wheel.

76919.q: What do children collect on the beach?
76919.e: Shell and beach: by the sea you find lots of pretty shells in the sand.
76919.m: You can collect shells on the beach.

76920.q: What is this person doing on the waves?
76920.e: Wave and surfer: you stand on a board and ride the waves. That is surfing.
76920.m: When you surf, you ride the waves.

76921.e: Sailing boat, waves and wind: the wind blows into the sail and drives the boat.
76921.m: A sailing boat moves with the wind.

76922.q: Which sea creature do these pictures make together?
76922.e: The sea and the hedgehog together make sea urchin, because ‘urchin’ is an old word for hedgehog. It has spines like a hedgehog.
76922.m: A sea urchin has sharp spines.

76923.q: Which animal lays its eggs in the sand on the beach?
76923.e: Turtle, eggs and beach: sea turtles come onto land and bury their eggs in the sand.
76923.m: Sea turtles lay their eggs in the sand.

76924.q: Which fish do these pictures make?
76924.e: Saw and fish together make sawfish. Its long snout looks like a saw.
76924.m: The sawfish has a snout like a saw.

76925.e: The salt shaker and the waves show it: there is a lot of salt dissolved in seawater. That is why it tastes salty.

76926.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76926.e: Air and bed together make airbed. You can lie on it in the water.
76926.m: An airbed is filled with air.

76927.q: What is it called when the sea rises and falls again?
76927.e: Waves, arrows up and down and the Moon: the Moon pulls on the water, so the sea rises and falls every day. These are called the tides, low tide and high tide.
76927.m: With the tides, the sea falls and rises.

76928.q: What do lots of families do at home in spring?
76928.e: Broom, window and tulip show the spring clean. After the winter, people clean their home thoroughly.
76928.m: In a spring clean, the whole home is cleaned.

76929.q: What do you do in the vegetable garden in spring?
76929.e: Gardener, seedling and carrot show it: in spring you sow seeds. In summer and autumn you can harvest the vegetables.
76929.m: In spring, you sow the seeds in the garden.

76930.q: What do these pictures show in order?
76930.e: First there is a seed, then a seedling and finally a flower. That is how a plant grows.
76930.m: A beautiful flower can grow from a tiny seed.

76931.q: What do lots of birds do early in the morning in spring?
76931.e: The bird, the musical notes and the tree show a singing bird. In spring, lots of birds sing early in the morning.
76931.m: In spring, you hear lots of birds singing in the morning.

76932.q: What do frogs lay in the water in spring?
76932.e: Frog, eggs and water show it: in spring, frogs lay lots of small eggs in the water. These eggs are called spawn.

76933.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76933.e: Cherry and blossom together make cherry blossom. In spring, cherry trees are full of white or pink blossom.
76933.m: In summer, the cherry blossom turns into a cherry.

76934.q: What happens to the clocks in spring?
76934.e: The alarm clock and the arrow pointing forward show it: the clocks go forward. In Switzerland, summer time begins on the last Sunday in March.
76934.m: In spring, we put the clocks forward one hour.

76935.q: Which season do these pictures show?
76935.e: Tulips are flowering, and bees and butterflies are flying again. That fits spring.
76935.m: In spring, nature wakes up after the winter.

76936.q: What protects your head from the sun in summer?
76936.e: Hat and sun show it: a sun hat gives your head shade and protects it from too much sun.
76936.m: A sun hat protects your head from the sun.

76937.q: Which season do these pictures show?
76937.e: Ice cream, beach and hot sun fit summer. That is when it is warmest.

76938.q: In which month is the longest day of the year?
76938.e: Sun, clock and moon ask about the length of the day. Around 21 June, the sun shines longest where we live.
76938.m: The days are longest in June.

76939.q: What do farmers do in the meadow in summer?
76939.e: Cow, grass and sun show the hay harvest. The grass is cut and dried in the sun.
76939.m: In summer, farmers make hay for the winter.

76940.q: What begins when school closes in summer?
76940.e: The school building, the lock and the sun show it: school is closed in summer. Then it is the summer holidays, the longest holidays of the year.
76940.m: The summer holidays are the longest school holidays.

76941.q: What is especially important on very hot days?
a: Lying in the sun for a long time
76941.e: The sweating face, water and a cup show it: in hot weather, the body needs lots to drink.
76941.m: In hot weather, you should drink lots of water.

76942.q: Which device shows how hot it is?
76942.e: Thermometer and sun: the thermometer measures the temperature. In summer it often rises above 30 degrees.
76942.m: You measure the temperature with a thermometer.

76943.q: What can you often see in the night sky in August?
76943.e: A shooting star and the moon show the night sky. Around the middle of August, you can see especially many shooting stars.
76943.m: In August you can see lots of shooting stars at night.

76944.q: Which shoes do people like to wear on the beach in summer?
76944.e: Beach and open sandals show flip-flops. They are airy and quick to put on.
76944.m: In summer, people like to wear flip-flops on the beach.

76945.q: Which season do these pictures show?
76945.e: Colourful falling leaves and rain fit autumn.
76945.m: In autumn, the leaves turn colourful and fall from the trees.

76946.q: What do children like doing in autumn when it is windy?
76946.e: Wind and a kite show it: the autumn wind carries the kite high into the air.
76946.m: Windy autumn days are good for flying a kite.

76947.q: What is harvested in the vineyards in autumn?
76947.e: Grapes, a basket and autumn leaves show the grape harvest. In autumn, the grapes on the vines are ripe.
76947.m: In autumn, the grapes are harvested in the vineyards.

76948.q: What does this animal do in autumn?
76948.e: The squirrel collects nuts and hides them. That way it finds food in winter.
76948.m: In autumn, the squirrel hides nuts for the winter.

76949.q: What do you do in the garden in autumn with all the leaves?
76949.e: Autumn leaves, a broom and a house with a garden show it: the fallen leaves are raked up.
76949.m: In autumn, you rake up the leaves.

76950.q: Where do lots of birds fly in autumn?
76950.e: The birds, the Earth and the sun show it: migrating birds fly to warmer countries. There they find enough food in winter.
76950.m: Migrating birds fly to the warm south in autumn.

76951.q: What weather is there often in the morning in autumn on the Swiss Plateau?
76951.e: The grey band of cloud and the morning show fog. In autumn, there is often thick fog on the Swiss Plateau.
76951.m: In autumn, it is often foggy in the morning.

76952.q: Which warm treat is sold at street stalls in autumn?
76952.e: Chestnut, fire and paper bag show roasted chestnuts, called Marroni in Switzerland. You buy them warm in a paper bag.
76952.m: Hot roasted chestnuts warm your hands in autumn.

76953.q: What is used to heat the house here in winter?
76953.e: Fire, a log and a house show it: wood burns in the stove and warms the house.
76953.m: You can heat a stove with wood.

76954.q: What do you often have to scrape off the car window in winter?
76954.e: Car, ice and window show it: on cold nights, the windscreen freezes. In the morning you scrape the ice off.
76954.m: In winter, you scrape ice off the windscreen.

76955.q: How many points does a snowflake usually have?
76955.e: With a magnifying glass you can see that snowflakes usually have six points. That is because of the shape of the ice crystals.
76955.m: A snowflake usually has six points.

76956.q: What is a house made of blocks of snow called?
76956.e: Ice, blocks and house show an igloo. It is built from firm blocks of snow.
76956.m: An igloo is a house made of snow.

76957.q: What forms on the window when it is very cold?
76957.e: Ice, flower and window together make ice flowers. Frozen moisture forms patterns like flowers on the window.
76957.m: Ice flowers form when it is very cold outside.

76958.q: Which winter sport in the forest do these pictures show?
76958.e: Long skis, a forest and snow show cross-country skiing. You glide on narrow skis along flat tracks.
76958.m: In cross-country skiing you glide on narrow skis along the track.

76959.q: How can you help birds in winter?
a: With a ball to play with
76959.e: A bird, snow and sunflower seeds show: in winter birds find little food. Seeds in a bird feeder help them. Birds cannot digest milk.
76959.m: In winter birds are happy to get food.

76960.q: At what temperature does water freeze into ice?
76960.e: Water, a thermometer and ice show: at 0 degrees Celsius water turns into ice.
76960.m: Water freezes into ice at 0 degrees.

76961.q: Which cake with a hidden figure do people eat in Switzerland on 6 January?
76961.e: A crown, bread and the number 6 show Three Kings' Day. Whoever finds the little figure in the Three Kings cake gets to wear the crown.
76961.m: On 6 January people in Switzerland eat Three Kings cake.

76962.e: Fir branches and four candles make an Advent wreath. Each Sunday in Advent you light one more candle.
76962.m: The Advent wreath has four candles for the four Sundays of Advent.

76963.e: A calendar, little doors and chocolate show an Advent calendar. From 1 to 24 December you open one little door each day.
76963.m: With an Advent calendar you open one little door every day.

76964.q: Which story do these pictures show?
76964.e: A baby, a star, an ox and straw show the manger in the stable in Bethlehem. Christmas remembers this.
76964.m: At Christmas Christians remember the birth of Jesus.

76965.q: What do many families in Switzerland bake before Christmas?
76965.e: Biscuits, a star cutter and a bowl show Christmas baking. Typical ones are butter biscuits, cinnamon stars and Brunsli.
76965.m: Before Christmas many families bake biscuits.

76966.q: What do many people do together at Christmas?
76966.e: Musical notes, a Christmas tree and a bell show: people sing carols like “Silent Night”.
76966.m: At Christmas many families sing songs together.

76967.q: What is the evening of 24 December called?
76967.e: A Christmas tree, night and family show Christmas Eve. Many families celebrate together then.
76967.m: On Christmas Eve many families celebrate Christmas.

76968.q: Who brings the presents at Christmas in many Swiss families?
76968.e: The angel with the present shows the Christ Child. In many Swiss families it brings the presents.
76968.m: In many Swiss families the Christ Child brings the presents.

76969.q: Which festival do these pictures show?
76969.e: Eggs, spring flowers and chicks belong to Easter.
76969.m: Easter is celebrated in spring with colourful eggs.

76970.q: What do you do with these things before Easter?
76970.e: An egg, paint and a brush show: you paint the eggs in bright colours.
76970.m: Before Easter you paint eggs in bright colours.

76971.q: According to tradition, who hides the Easter eggs?
76971.e: The rabbit with a basket and eggs is the Easter Bunny. It hides the eggs in the garden.
76971.m: The Easter Bunny hides the Easter eggs.

76972.q: What do children do on Easter morning?
76972.e: An egg, a magnifying glass and a garden show the egg hunt. The children look for the hidden eggs.
76972.m: On Easter morning children look for the hidden eggs.

76973.q: Which Easter custom do these pictures show?
76973.e: Two eggs knock together. In egg tapping, the person whose egg does not break wins.
76973.m: In egg tapping you knock two eggs against each other.

76974.q: Which Easter bake do these pictures show?
76974.e: A sheep and a cake together make the Easter lamb. It is a cake in the shape of a lamb.
76974.m: The Easter lamb is a cake shaped like a lamb.

76975.q: What can you use to dye Easter eggs naturally?
76975.e: An onion and an egg show: if you boil eggs with onion skins, they turn brown to reddish.
76975.m: Onion skins dye eggs a lovely brown.

76976.q: What decides on which Sunday Easter is celebrated?
a: The first full moon in spring
The longest day of the year
The first new moon of the year
76976.e: Easter is on the first Sunday after the first full moon in spring. That is why Easter falls on a different date every year.
76976.m: The date of Easter depends on the full moon in spring.

76977.q: How often a year do you have a birthday?
76977.e: A cake, a calendar and the number 1: you have a birthday exactly once every year.
76977.m: You have a birthday once every year.

76978.q: What is the birthday child doing here?
76978.e: A cake, a candle and wind show: the candles on the cake are being blown out. While doing so, you may make a silent wish.
76978.m: When you blow out the candles, you may make a wish.

76979.q: Which song do many people sing with these pictures?
76979.e: Music, a cake and clapping show the birthday song. Many people sing “Happy Birthday”.
76979.m: On birthdays people often sing “Happy Birthday”.

76980.q: Which birthday game do these pictures show?
76980.e: A pot, a spoon and covered eyes show hit the pot. Blindfolded, you look for a pot with a surprise under it.
76980.m: In hit the pot you search for a pot while blindfolded.

76981.q: Which game do these pictures show?
76981.e: Chairs, music and running show musical chairs. When the music stops, everyone looks for a chair.
76981.m: In musical chairs there is always one chair too few.

76982.q: What do you send out before a birthday party?
76982.e: A letter, a balloon and a party show an invitation. With it you invite guests to the party.
76982.m: With an invitation you ask guests to come to the party.

76983.q: How old is the child turning if each candle counts as one year?
76983.e: There are 5 candles on the cake. Each candle stands for one year, so the child is turning 5.
76983.m: A birthday cake often has one candle for each year.

76984.q: What does the birthday child often wear at nursery school?
76984.e: A crown, a cake and a child show the birthday crown. With it the birthday child is king or queen for a day.
76984.m: With the birthday crown the child is king for a day.

76985.q: Who brings children in Switzerland nuts and tangerines?
76985.e: The man with a beard, nuts and tangerines is Samichlaus, the Swiss St Nicholas. He visits children at the beginning of December.
76985.m: Samichlaus brings nuts, tangerines and gingerbread.

76986.q: On which day is Samichlaus Day?
76986.e: A calendar, the number 6 and snow show 6 December. That day is Samichlaus Day.

76987.e: A sack with nuts, tangerines and gingerbread is the Samichlaus sack. Samichlaus brings it.
76987.m: The Samichlaus sack holds nuts, tangerines and gingerbread.

76988.q: What is the name of Samichlaus's companion dressed in dark clothes?
76988.e: The dark colour, the bundle of twigs and the lantern show Schmutzli. He goes with Samichlaus in a dark coat.

76989.q: What does Samichlaus bring with him on his visit?
76989.e: A book and a pen show Samichlaus's big book. It says what the children did well during the year and what they did not.
76989.m: Samichlaus's big book says what the children have done.

76990.q: What do many children recite to Samichlaus?
76990.e: Speaking, text and sound show a little rhyme. Many children recite a short poem to Samichlaus.
76990.m: You recite a little poem to Samichlaus.

76991.q: Which parade in Küssnacht am Rigi is meant?
76991.e: Glowing lanterns, bells and people show the Klausjagen. In Küssnacht many people walk through the village with big cowbells and glowing Iffelen, huge lantern hats.
76991.m: At the Klausjagen in Küssnacht the Iffelen glow and the cowbells ring.

76992.q: What do some children put outside the door on the evening before Samichlaus Day?
76992.e: A boot, chocolate and night show: you put a boot outside. In the morning it is filled with sweets.
76992.m: Some children find sweets in their boot on Samichlaus Day.

76993.q: What do some people collect in the forest in autumn?
76993.e: A mushroom, a forest and a basket show mushroom picking. Always have picked mushrooms checked by a mushroom inspector.
76993.m: Always take picked mushrooms to a mushroom inspector.

76994.q: Which late-winter festival do these pictures show?
76994.e: Costumes, a party and winter show carnival, called Fasnacht in Switzerland. It takes place in February or March.
76994.m: At carnival many people dress up.

76995.q: Which loud carnival music do these pictures show?
76995.e: A trumpet, a drum and music show a Guggenmusik band. It plays loudly and sometimes deliberately out of tune.
76995.m: A Guggenmusik band plays loudly at carnival.

76996.q: What are these colourful bits of paper called in Basel?
76996.e: The colourful bits of paper are confetti. In Basel they are called Räppli.
76996.m: In Basel confetti is called Räppli.

76997.q: What is the start of Basel carnival in the middle of the night called?
76997.e: Night, lanterns and drums show the Morgestraich. At 4 o'clock in the morning the lights in Basel go out and the lanterns light up.
76997.m: The Morgestraich in Basel begins at 4 o'clock in the morning.

76998.q: What is a carnival mask called in Basel?
76998.e: The two masks show a Larve. That is what the big carnival mask is called in Basel.
76998.m: In Basel the carnival mask is called a Larve.

76999.q: Which warm soup do people eat at the Basel Morgestraich?
76999.e: Grain stands for flour, together with the soup and the night. Early in the morning the flour soup warms up the carnival-goers.
76999.m: At the Morgestraich in Basel people eat flour soup.

77000.q: What do many children wear at carnival?
77000.e: A princess, a hero and a fairy are disguises. At carnival children put on costumes like these.
77000.m: At carnival many children wear a costume.

77001.q: Which thin pastry with icing sugar is eaten at carnival?
77001.e: Pastry, sweets and glitter show Fasnachtschüechli. They are thin, crispy and sprinkled with icing sugar.
77001.m: At carnival people eat crispy Fasnachtschüechli.

77002.q: Which autumn festival do these pictures show?
77002.e: A bat, a full moon and sweets go with Halloween. Children dress up in spooky costumes and collect sweets.
77002.m: At Halloween children dress up in spooky costumes.

77003.q: What colour are most Halloween pumpkins?
77003.e: The pumpkin and the colour palette ask about the colour. Halloween pumpkins are usually orange.

77004.q: What do children say at the front door at Halloween?
77004.e: A door, sweets and a child show the Halloween custom. The children ring the bell and ask for sweets.
77004.m: At Halloween children go from door to door asking for sweets.

77005.e: A calendar, a bat and autumn leaves show a day in autumn. Halloween is on 31 October.

77006.q: Which costume do these pictures show?
77006.e: A woman with a pointed hat, a broom and the moon show a witch. It is a popular Halloween costume.
77006.m: The witch is a popular Halloween costume.

77007.q: Which costume can you make from this?
77007.e: A white sheet with eye holes cut out turns into a ghost.
77007.m: An old sheet quickly becomes a ghost.

77008.q: Which country does the Halloween custom originally come from?
77008.e: The shamrock and the island stand for Ireland. Emigrants took the custom from there to America.

77009.q: What do you carve into a hollowed-out pumpkin at Halloween?
77009.e: A candle, a pumpkin and a knife show: you hollow out the pumpkin, carve a face into it and put a candle inside.
77009.m: At Halloween pumpkins glow with carved faces.

77010.q: When can you see something like this in the sky?
a: When there is sun and rain at once
77010.e: A rainbow appears when the sun is shining and it is raining at the same time.
77010.m: A rainbow needs sun and rain.

77011.q: How many colours do people usually count in a rainbow?
77011.e: People usually count 7 colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
77011.m: A rainbow usually has seven colours.

77012.q: Which colour is at the very top of a rainbow?
77012.e: In a rainbow red is at the very top, on the outside. Violet is at the very bottom, on the inside.
77012.m: In a rainbow red is usually at the very top.

77013.q: Where is the sun when you see a rainbow?
77013.e: You only see a rainbow with the sun at your back. The rain is in front of you.
77013.m: When you see a rainbow, the sun is at your back.

77014.q: According to an old story, what lies at the end of the rainbow?
77014.e: In an old story from Ireland, a leprechaun hides a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow. But nobody can find it.
77014.m: A pot of gold is said to lie at the end of the rainbow.

77015.q: How can you make a small rainbow yourself in the garden?
a: With water from the hose in the sun
With a torch in the dark
With a mirror in the cellar
77015.e: Water spray, the sun and a garden show: tiny water drops in sunlight make a small rainbow.
77015.m: With water drops and sunshine you can make a rainbow.

77016.q: What can split white light into rainbow colours?
77016.e: The lamp and the triangle show light and a prism. A glass prism splits white light into many colours.
77016.m: A prism splits light into bright colours.

77017.q: What does sunlight shine through when a rainbow forms?
77017.e: The sun shines through lots of tiny raindrops. This splits its light into bright colours.
77017.m: Raindrops turn sunlight into bright colours.

77018.e: Two arcs one above the other are a double rainbow. In the second, fainter arc the colours are the other way round.
77018.m: In a double rainbow the colours of the second arc are reversed.

77019.q: What weather do these pictures show?
77019.e: Lightning, rain and dark clouds show a thunderstorm.
77019.m: In a thunderstorm there is lightning and thunder.

77020.q: What do you notice first in a thunderstorm?
77020.e: First you see the lightning, and after a while you hear the thunder. Light is much faster than sound.
77020.m: You always see the lightning before the thunder.

77021.q: You count 3 seconds between lightning and thunder. Roughly how far away is the storm?
77021.e: Sound takes about 3 seconds to travel 1 kilometre. So at 3 seconds, the storm is about 1 kilometre away.
77021.m: Three seconds between lightning and thunder mean about one kilometre.

77022.q: Where should you not stand during a thunderstorm?
77022.e: A tree, lightning and a no sign show: it is dangerous under a lone tree. Lightning often strikes tall trees.
77022.m: In a thunderstorm never stand under a lone tree.

77023.q: Where are you well protected during a thunderstorm?
77023.e: A car, lightning and a thumbs-up show: you are safe in a car. The metal body carries the lightning around the outside.
77023.m: In a thunderstorm you are well protected in a car.

77024.q: What are many dogs afraid of during a thunderstorm?
77024.e: A storm cloud, a dog and a frightened face: many dogs are scared by the loud thunder.
77024.m: Many dogs are afraid of loud thunder.

77025.q: What sometimes falls from the sky in heavy thunderstorms?
77025.e: The storm cloud and the white balls show hail. Hailstones are balls of ice.
77025.m: Hail is made of small balls of ice.

77026.q: What does a thunder cloud look like?
77026.e: The cloud, the arrow pointing up and the dark colour show: thunder clouds tower up high and turn dark.
77026.m: Thunder clouds are enormously tall and dark.

77027.q: What should you do if a thunderstorm comes while you are swimming in a lake?
a: Get out of the water at once
Swim to the middle of the lake
77027.e: A swimmer, lightning and running show: you leave the water at once. Water conducts the electricity of the lightning.
77027.m: In a thunderstorm get out of the water at once.

77028.e: A toothbrush, a tooth and sparkles show: the teeth are being brushed clean here.
77028.m: We brush our teeth with a toothbrush.

77029.q: According to these pictures, when do you brush your teeth?
77029.e: The sun stands for the morning, the moon for the evening. In between is the toothbrush.
77029.m: We brush our teeth in the morning and in the evening.

77030.q: How long should brushing take here?
77030.e: The stopwatch and the number two show the brushing time. Dentists recommend about two minutes.
77030.m: Brushing your teeth properly takes about two minutes.

77031.q: What is happening to the tooth here?
77031.e: Lots of sweets and a sad face: sugar harms your teeth and holes can form.
77031.m: Too much sugar can make holes in your teeth.

77032.q: Where is the child going here?
77032.e: A tooth and a doctor show a visit to the dentist.
77032.m: The dentist checks whether your teeth are healthy.

77033.q: What do you do here after brushing?
77033.e: Water and an open mouth after the toothbrush: you rinse your mouth.
77033.m: After brushing I rinse my mouth with water.

77034.q: Which morning snack here is good for your teeth?
77034.e: A tooth, an apple and a carrot go together: crunchy fruit and vegetables have little sugar and are good for your teeth.
77034.m: An apple is a tooth-friendly snack.

77035.q: What is happening here in the story?
a: The Tooth Fairy collects the baby tooth
77035.e: A tooth, a fairy and a coin: in the story the Tooth Fairy collects the baby tooth and leaves a coin.
77035.m: When a baby tooth falls out, the Tooth Fairy comes in the story.

77036.q: What should you not forget when brushing?
77036.e: The toothbrush goes round to lots of teeth. You brush every tooth, including the ones at the back.
77036.m: When brushing, every tooth gets a turn.

77037.e: Eggs, flour from grain, butter and a bowl are ingredients for a cake.
77037.m: For a cake you need eggs, flour and butter.

77038.q: Where does the mixture go here?
77038.e: Fire and a kitchen timer show heat and baking time. The mixture goes into the hot oven.
77038.m: In the hot oven the mixture turns into a cake.

77039.q: Why do you need gloves here?
a: It is cold in the kitchen
77039.e: A glove, fire and a cake: with oven gloves you take the hot tray out of the oven.
77039.m: Oven gloves protect your hands from heat.

77040.q: How old is the child turning in this picture?
77040.e: There are three candles on the cake. Each candle counts as one year.
77040.m: A birthday cake has one candle for each year.

77041.q: What kind of cake is this?
77041.e: Chocolate and a cake together make a chocolate cake.
77041.m: A chocolate cake is baked with chocolate.

77042.q: What does the child here like to lick after baking?
77042.e: A bowl, a spoon, a tongue and a happy face show: the child licks the spoon with cake mixture.
77042.m: After stirring, many children like to lick the mixing spoon.

77043.e: An apple and a cake with a rim show an apple tart, called Apfelwähe in Switzerland.
77043.m: An apple tart is a flat cake with apples.

77044.q: What is happening here in the bowl?
77044.e: Eggs, a bowl, a spoon and a swirl show: the eggs are being whisked.
77044.m: For the mixture, the eggs are whisked well.

77045.q: What is happening here to the little cakes?
77045.e: Muffins, colours and sugar sprinkles show: the muffins are being decorated in bright colours.
77045.m: We decorate the muffins with colourful sprinkles.

77046.e: A child, snowflakes and a snowman: the child is building a snowman.
77046.m: In winter children love building a snowman.

77047.q: What do you use here for the nose?
77047.e: A carrot and a nose go together: the snowman gets a carrot for a nose.
77047.m: A snowman often has a carrot for a nose.

77048.q: What do you use here for the snowman's arms?
77048.e: A snowman, a tree and an arm show: for the arms you stick two branches from a tree into the snowman.
77048.m: Two sticks become the snowman's arms.

77049.q: How many balls is this snowman made of?
77049.e: Next to the snowman there are three white balls: big at the bottom, medium in the middle, small on top.
77049.m: A snowman often has three balls.

77050.q: What is the snowman getting here?
77050.e: Next to the snowman there are a scarf and a hat. He is dressed with them.
77050.m: With a scarf and a hat the snowman looks funny.

77051.q: What does the child put on here for building?
77051.e: Snow, a shivering face and gloves show: in cold snow you need warm gloves.
77051.m: In the snow warm gloves protect your hands.

77052.q: What is the child riding down the hill here?
77052.e: A child, a sledge, a snowman and falling snow show: in the snow the child rides a sledge down the hill.
77052.m: In winter you can ride a sledge down the hill.

77053.q: What do people often use here for the eyes?
77053.e: The black dots are small stones or pieces of coal. They become the eyes.
77053.m: Small dark stones become the snowman's eyes.

77054.q: How does the snowball here get bigger?
a: You roll it in the snow
You put it in the sun
77054.e: The ball turns through the snow and gets bigger. As it rolls, new snow sticks to it.
77054.m: A snowball gets bigger and bigger as you roll it.

77055.e: A shopping trolley, food and a receipt show: someone is doing the shopping here.
77055.m: We buy food in the shop.

77056.q: Where in the shop are you here?
77056.e: Money and a receipt show paying. You pay at the till.
77056.m: We pay for our shopping at the till.

77057.q: What helps here with the shopping?
77057.e: A note with milk, bread and cheese: the shopping list says what you want to buy.
77057.m: With a shopping list you forget nothing.

77058.q: What are you doing here for the environment?
a: Using the bag again and again
Taking lots of new plastic bags
77058.e: The bag, the arrow sign for “again and again” and the Earth show: using a bag many times protects the environment.
77058.m: You can use a shopping bag many times.

77059.q: What are you doing with the fruit here?
77059.e: There are scales next to the fruit. The fruit is weighed so that you know the price.
77059.m: We weigh the fruit on the scales.

77060.q: What is the child buying with their money here?
77060.e: Coins and an ice cream cone: the child is buying an ice cream.
77060.m: With pocket money you can buy yourself an ice cream.

77061.q: Where do you buy these things?
77061.e: The baker makes bread and croissants. You buy them at the bakery.
77061.m: At the bakery you can get bread and croissants.

77062.q: Which shop are you in here?
77062.e: You buy plasters, a thermometer and ointment at the chemist's.
77062.m: At the chemist's you can get plasters and thermometers.

77063.q: Where is the shopping being done here?
77063.e: Vegetables, berries, a sunshade and a farmer show a market stall outdoors.
77063.m: At the market farmers sell fresh vegetables.

77064.e: A train, a suitcase and waving goodbye: someone is leaving by train.
77064.m: You can travel a long way by train.

77065.q: Where do you wait for the train here?
77065.e: A person standing, the station and an hourglass show: you wait on the platform at the station until the train comes.
77065.m: You wait on the platform until the train comes in.

77066.q: Why is the person running here?
a: The train is about to leave
77066.e: A station, a clock and a running person: they are late and want to catch the train.
77066.m: If you are at the station early, you do not have to run.

77067.q: What is the train going into here?
77067.e: A train, a mountain and a hole show: the train goes through a tunnel in the mountain. Switzerland has many railway tunnels, for example at the Gotthard.
77067.m: A tunnel takes the train right through the mountain.

77068.q: What kind of train is this?
77068.e: An old locomotive with lots of smoke and steam is a steam engine.
77068.m: A steam engine runs on steam from hot water.

77069.q: What can you see here from the train window?
77069.e: Through the window you can see a cow and mountains, as you often do in Switzerland.
77069.m: From the train window in Switzerland you often see mountains.

77070.q: What is the train doing at the station here?
77070.e: The stop sign at the station shows: the train stops so that people can get on and off.
77070.m: The train stops at the station.

77071.e: A mountain railway, a mountain and snow show: the train is going up the mountain.
77071.m: A mountain railway takes you up a mountain.

77072.e: A pot plant and water drops show: the plant is being watered.
77072.m: Plants need water, so we water them.

77073.q: What is happening to the plant here?
77073.e: With sun and water the little seedling becomes a big flower.
77073.m: With light and water a plant grows.

77074.q: What is wrong with the plant here?
77074.e: Lots of sun and a wilted flower: the plant has dried out and needs water.

77075.q: Who is watering the flowers here?
77075.e: There is a rain cloud above the tulips. The rain waters the flowers.
77075.m: The rain waters the flowers in the garden.

a: The seed is becoming a plant
The plant is becoming a seed
The water is turning into ice
77076.e: A seed gets water and a small seedling grows from it.
77076.m: A new plant can grow from a seed.

77077.q: What is growing in the pot here?
77077.e: Next to the watered pot is a tomato. You can also grow tomatoes in a pot on the balcony.
77077.m: Tomatoes also grow in a pot on the balcony.

77078.q: How often does this plant need water?
a: All the time, it stands in water
77078.e: A cactus stores water inside itself. That is why it only rarely needs water.
77078.m: A cactus needs only a little water.

77079.q: When is the watering done here in summer?
a: In the middle of the night
77079.e: The sunrise shows early morning. It is cool then and the water does not evaporate so quickly.
77079.m: In summer it is best to water early in the morning.

a: A school trip to the museum
77080.e: A basket, sandwiches and a tree show: people are eating outdoors here.
77080.m: At a picnic we eat outdoors.

77081.q: Who turns up uninvited to the picnic here?
77081.e: Ants are crawling next to the basket. They like the crumbs from the picnic.
77081.m: Ants love looking for crumbs at a picnic.

77082.q: What is happening at the picnic here?
77082.e: A rain cloud and an umbrella show: the picnic is getting wet.
77082.m: When it rains, you need an umbrella at a picnic.

77083.q: What do you do here after the picnic?
77083.e: A basket, a bin and a tree: after the picnic the rubbish goes in the bin so that nature stays clean.
77083.m: After the picnic we take our rubbish with us.

77084.q: What are people playing here after the picnic?
77084.e: A basket, a flying disc and a dog show: on the meadow people throw a frisbee to each other and the dog runs along.
77084.m: A big meadow is a good place to play frisbee.

77085.q: What is happening at the picnic here?
77085.e: Fire, a sausage and a tree show: sausages are grilled over a fire in the forest, in Switzerland often cervelats.
77085.m: We love grilling a cervelat over the fire.

77086.q: What are people sitting on here at the picnic?
77086.e: The red and white squares show a checked blanket on the flower meadow.
77086.m: At a picnic we sit on a blanket.

77087.q: Who would like a taste of the sweet juice here?
77087.e: A bee is buzzing next to the juice. Bees like sweet things.
77087.m: Bees are attracted by sweet drinks.

77088.e: A tent in the forest at night: people are camping and spending the night outdoors.
77088.m: When camping we sleep outdoors in a tent.

77089.q: What do people do here in the evening?
77089.e: A tent, a fire and a guitar show: people make music and sing round the campfire.
77089.m: We love singing together round the campfire.

77090.q: What do you sleep in here in the tent?
77090.e: A tent, the moon and a sleeping face: in the tent you sleep in a warm sleeping bag.
77090.m: In the tent we sleep in a sleeping bag.

77091.q: What keeps the tent in place in the wind here?
77091.e: A tent, a rope and wind show: guy ropes and pegs in the ground hold the tent firmly.
77091.m: Pegs and guy ropes hold the tent firmly.

77092.q: What do you need here at night?
77092.e: Next to the tent in the dark night is a torch. With it you can see in the dark.
77092.m: A torch helps in the dark.

77093.q: Which animal is flying round the tent here at night?
77093.e: A bat is flying next to the tent at night. Bats hunt insects at night.
77093.m: Bats fly at night and hunt insects.

77094.e: A tent, a mountain and a walking boot show a tent in the mountains.
77094.m: With walking boots you go camping in the mountains.

77095.q: What can you see here above the campsite?
77095.e: Lots of stars are shining in the night sky above the campsite.
77095.m: At night the stars shine in the sky.

77096.e: A fishing rod, a fish and water show: someone is fishing here.
77096.m: You catch fish with a fishing rod.

77097.q: What do you put on the hook here?
77097.e: Between the rod and the fish there is a worm. It lures the fish onto the hook.

77098.q: What do you do here with the fish that is too small?
a: Put it back in the water
77098.e: The arrow back to the water shows: fish that are too small are put back so that they can keep growing.
77098.m: Fish that are too small go back into the water.

77099.q: What do you need here when fishing?
77099.e: An hourglass and a sleepy face show: you have to wait a long time. Fishing takes patience.
77099.m: When fishing you have to wait patiently.

77100.q: What is happening to the fish here?
77100.e: After it is caught, the fish goes into the frying pan.
77100.m: A fresh fish can be fried in the pan.

77101.e: A bear is standing by the river catching a fish. Bears catch fish with their paws.
77101.m: Bears catch fish with their paws.

77102.q: Where are people fishing from here?
77102.e: A rod, a rowing boat and a lake show: here people fish from a boat.
77102.m: You can also fish from a boat.

77103.q: Where is the fishing taking place here?
77103.e: Ice and a hole show: you fish through a hole in the ice of a frozen lake.
77103.m: In ice fishing you fish through a hole in the ice.

77104.e: A bed, the moon and a tired face show: it is evening and time to go to sleep.
77104.m: In the evening we go to bed.

77105.q: What is happening here before sleep?
77105.e: A book, a bed and a child: before sleep a bedtime story is read aloud.
77105.m: A bedtime story helps you fall asleep.

77106.q: Who is sleeping in the bed too here?
77106.e: There is a teddy bear next to the bed. Many children cuddle it when they sleep.
77106.m: Many children sleep with a teddy bear.

77107.q: What do you do here before going to sleep?
77107.e: A lamp, a finger on the switch and darkness: the light is being switched off.
77107.m: To sleep we switch off the light.

77108.q: What do people often do here before going to bed?
77108.e: A bath and soap before bed show: before sleep you have a bath.
77108.m: A warm bath in the evening makes you nice and sleepy.

77109.q: What is happening here during sleep?
77109.e: A sleeping face and a thought bubble with a unicorn show a dream.
77109.m: Sometimes we dream while we sleep.

77110.q: What is happening here in the morning?
a: The child is going for a swim
77110.e: An alarm clock, the sun, a bed and a yawn show: it is morning and the child is waking up.
77110.m: In the morning the alarm clock rings to get you up.

77111.q: What time does the child go to bed here?
77111.e: The clock shows eight o'clock. At eight o'clock in the evening the child goes to bed.
77111.m: Children need enough sleep and go to bed early.

77112.e: A ball comes out of the present and the child is happy: the child is unwrapping a present.
77112.m: When unwrapping, you are excited to see what is inside.

77113.q: When do you unwrap these presents?
77113.e: A Christmas tree with a star and presents underneath: that is Christmas.
77113.m: At Christmas there are presents under the Christmas tree.

a: It is the first day of school
77114.e: A cake, a balloon and a present belong to a birthday party.
77114.m: On birthdays there is often cake and presents.

77115.q: What do you say here after unwrapping?
77115.e: The folded hands and the smile show gratitude. For a present you say thank you.
77115.m: For a present we say thank you.

77116.q: What is still a secret here before unwrapping?
77116.e: A present, a question mark and a thoughtful face: you do not yet know what is inside.

77117.q: What was in the present here?
77117.e: Next to the present is a puzzle piece. The child got a jigsaw puzzle.
77117.m: You put a jigsaw together piece by piece.

77118.q: How many presents are there here?
77118.e: Count the parcels: one, two, three, four, five.
77118.m: Here there are five presents to unwrap.

77119.e: Parents and a child, a present and confetti show a family celebration.
77119.m: Celebrating with your family is fun.

77120.e: A dog, a child, a tree and footprints show a walk with the dog.
77120.m: A dog needs a walk every day.

77121.q: What do you do here with the dog poo?
a: Pick it up with a bag
77121.e: A dog, poo and a bag show: you pick up the poo with a bag and put it in the bin.
77121.m: We pick up dog poo with a bag.

77122.q: What does the dog here like to play?
77122.e: A dog, a ball and running show: the dog fetches the ball that was thrown.
77122.m: Many dogs love fetching a ball.

77123.q: Where must the dog be on a lead?
77123.e: Traffic lights and a car show a road. There the dog belongs on a lead so that it does not run in front of a car.
77123.m: By the road the dog stays on its lead.

77124.q: What does the dog need here after the walk?
77124.e: A dog, water and a bowl show: after running the dog is thirsty.
77124.m: After the walk the dog drinks fresh water.

77125.q: What is the dog doing here?
77125.e: A dog, a cat and a cloud of dust show: the dog is running after the cat.

77126.q: What is the dog doing at the tree here?
77126.e: A dog, a nose and a tree show: the dog is sniffing the tree. Its nose has a very good sense of smell.
77126.m: A dog explores the world with its nose.

77127.q: Which command is the dog learning here?
77127.e: A dog, a chair and an arrow pointing down show: the dog should sit down. The command is “Sit”.
77127.m: On the command “Sit” the dog sits down.

77128.q: Which Swiss dish do these pictures show?
77128.e: With fondue you dip pieces of bread into melted cheese in a caquelon pot. Those are exactly the things in the picture.
77128.m: Fondue is eaten with bread and melted cheese.

77129.q: Which cheese dish do these pictures show?
77129.e: With raclette, cheese is melted and eaten with potatoes. Fondue goes with bread, not potatoes.
77129.m: With raclette you eat melted cheese with potatoes.

77130.q: Which Swiss cheese do these pictures mean?
77130.e: The hole stands for the big holes. Emmental is famous for its big holes.

77131.q: Which animal here likes nibbling cheese?
77131.e: Cheese, a mouse and a happy face: in many stories the mouse nibbles the cheese.
77131.m: In picture books the mouse often nibbles cheese.

77132.q: What do these pictures show in order?
77132.e: The cow gives milk and the arrow points to the cheese. Cheese is made from milk.

77133.q: Which building do these pictures make together?
77133.e: A building where cheese is made is called a cheese dairy. That is where farmers take their milk.
77133.m: In the cheese dairy milk is made into cheese.

77134.q: Which Swiss dish do these pictures show?
77134.e: Älplermagronen are Alpine herdsman's macaroni with potatoes and cheese. They are often eaten with apple sauce.
77134.m: Älplermagronen are often eaten with apple sauce.

77135.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
77135.e: A person is making cheese from milk. This job is called cheesemaker.
77135.m: The cheesemaker turns milk into delicious cheese.

77136.q: Which kind of chocolate do these pictures show?
77136.e: Milk and chocolate together make milk chocolate. The Swiss Daniel Peter from Vevey made a famous milk chocolate in 1875.
77136.m: Milk chocolate was invented in Switzerland.

77137.q: Which chocolate do these pictures mean?
77137.e: Chocolate and nuts together make nut chocolate. It has whole or chopped nuts inside.

77138.q: Which hot drink do these pictures show?
77138.e: Chocolate, milk, heat and a cup together make a hot chocolate.
77138.m: Hot chocolate is made from milk and chocolate.

77139.e: The arrow points from the tree to the chocolate. Chocolate is made from the beans of the cocoa tree.
77139.m: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.

77140.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77140.e: Chocolate and factory make chocolate factory. There chocolate is made in large quantities.
77140.m: Chocolate is made in the chocolate factory.

77141.q: Which dessert do these pictures mean?
77141.e: Chocolate and the creamy pudding in the little bowl together make chocolate mousse.
77141.m: You eat chocolate mousse with a spoon.

77142.q: Which ice cream do these pictures show?
77142.e: Chocolate and ice cream together make chocolate ice cream. In Switzerland ice cream is called Glace.
77142.m: In Switzerland ice cream is called Glace.

77143.q: Which morning snack do these pictures mean?
77143.e: Bread and a piece of chocolate together make a Schoggibrot. In Switzerland chocolate is often called Schoggi.
77143.m: In Switzerland chocolate is called Schoggi.

77144.q: Which famous Swiss mountain do these pictures mean?
77144.e: The triangle shows a pointed pyramid. The Matterhorn near Zermatt has exactly this shape and is 4478 metres high.
77144.m: The Matterhorn looks like a pointed pyramid.

77145.q: Which word goes with these pictures?
77145.e: A person is climbing up a mountain. Someone who climbs mountains is a mountaineer.

77146.q: What stands on many mountain tops?
77146.e: On many summits in the Alps there is a cross. It is called a summit cross.
77146.m: There is a summit cross on many peaks.

77147.q: What are people doing here in the mountains?
77147.e: You need walking boots and a rucksack for hiking. There are many hiking trails in the Swiss mountains.
77147.m: For hiking you need good shoes.

77148.q: Which winter sport do these pictures mean?
77148.e: The person is skiing down the snowy mountain. That is skiing.
77148.m: In winter you can go skiing in the mountains.

77149.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77149.e: Mountain and hut together make mountain hut. Hikers can eat and sleep there.
77149.m: Hikers can stay the night in a mountain hut.

77150.q: What is the big mountain range in Switzerland shown in these pictures called?
77150.e: Many mountains together form a mountain range. The biggest mountain range in Switzerland is the Alps.
77150.m: The Alps are the biggest mountain range in Switzerland.

77151.q: What do you hear when you shout loudly like this in the mountains?
77151.e: The shout bounces off the rocks and comes back. That is called an echo.
77151.m: An echo is a shout that comes back.

77152.q: What is sliding down the mountain here?
77152.e: A lot of snow is sliding quickly down the mountain. That is an avalanche.
77152.m: An avalanche is snow sliding down a mountain.

77153.q: Where do many cows spend the summer?
77153.e: The cow is on a flower meadow high up in the mountains. In summer many cows graze on the alp, a high mountain pasture.
77153.m: In summer many cows are up on the alp.

77154.q: Which custom do these pictures mean?
a: Cows going up to the alp
Cows coming down from the alp
77154.e: The cows are going up into the mountains. That is the Alpaufzug at the beginning of summer.
77154.m: In the Alpaufzug the cows go up to the alp in early summer.

77155.q: Which custom do these pictures mean?
a: Cows coming down from the alp
Cows going up to the alp
77155.e: In autumn the cows come down from the alp into the valley. In the Alpabzug they are often decorated with flowers.
77155.m: In the Alpabzug the cows come down to the valley in autumn.

77156.q: What is the farmer doing here?
77156.e: The bucket under the cow catches the milk. The farmer is milking the cow.
77156.m: When milking, you get the milk out of the udder.

77157.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77157.e: A building for cows is called a cowshed. The cows sleep and eat there.
77157.m: The cows live in the cowshed.

77158.q: What does the cow here like to eat best?
77158.e: The cow eats plants. In the pasture it mainly eats grass.
77158.m: Cows eat grass in the pasture.

77159.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
77159.e: In summer the Alpine dairyman, called a Senn, looks after the cows on the alp and makes cheese from the milk there.
77159.m: The Alpine dairyman makes cheese up on the alp.

77160.q: What is the strongest cow called in the cow fights in Valais?
77160.e: The crown shows the winner. In the fights of the Hérens cows, the strongest cow is called the queen.
77160.m: In Valais the strongest cow is called the queen.

77161.q: What is made from the milk at the end here?
77161.e: The cow gives milk, and at the end you can see a piece of butter. Butter is made from the cream of the milk.

77162.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77162.e: A watch and a factory make watch factory. There are many watch factories in the Jura.
77162.m: Many watches are made in the Jura.

77163.q: Which clock do these pictures mean?
77163.e: On this clock a bird comes out and calls “cuckoo”. That is why it is called a cuckoo clock.
77163.m: A little bird comes out of the cuckoo clock.

77164.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77164.e: Sand and a clock together make a sand timer. In it, sand trickles from the top to the bottom.
77164.m: In a sand timer the sand trickles down.

77165.q: Which clock wakes you up here in the morning?
77165.e: Next to the bed a clock rings in the morning. That is the alarm clock.
77165.m: The alarm clock rings in the morning.

77166.q: Which clock measures here how fast someone runs?
77166.e: With a stopwatch you measure exactly how long a race takes.
77166.m: With a stopwatch you time a race.

77167.q: Which meal do these pictures mean?
77167.e: The clock shows twelve o'clock in the day and the plate shows food. That is lunch, called Zmittag in Switzerland.
77167.m: At twelve o'clock you have lunch.

77168.q: Which meal do these pictures mean?
77168.e: The clock shows four o'clock. In Switzerland the little snack in the afternoon is called Zvieri.
77168.m: At four o'clock there is the afternoon snack.

77169.q: What is the famous tower with a clock in Bern called?
77169.e: The bear stands for Bern. The Zytglogge is an old tower in Bern with a famous clock.
77169.m: The Zytglogge is a clock tower in Bern.

77170.q: Which watch do these pictures show?
77170.e: The watch is worn on the arm. That is why it is called a wristwatch.
77170.m: You wear a wristwatch on your wrist.

77171.q: Which red Swiss tool has all these parts in one?
77171.e: The red Swiss army knife has many tools, for example scissors and a screwdriver. It fits in your trouser pocket.
77171.m: The Swiss army knife has many tools in one.

77172.q: What can you do with these small scissors on the Swiss army knife?
77172.e: Scissors cut. With them you can, for example, cut paper.

77173.q: What do you use here to pull the wooden splinter out of your finger?
77173.e: Wood, a finger and a pained face show a splinter. You pull it out with the small tweezers that many Swiss army knives have.
77173.m: You carefully pull out a splinter with tweezers.

77174.q: Which country does the well-known red pocket knife come from?
77174.e: Mountains, cheese and chocolate stand for Switzerland. The red pocket knife comes from Switzerland.
77174.m: The red pocket knife is a well-known tool from Switzerland.

77175.q: Which tool do these pictures mean?
77175.e: The tin is being opened. For that you need a tin opener, which the Swiss army knife also has.
77175.m: You open a tin with a tin opener.

77176.q: Which symbol can you see on many Swiss army knives?
77176.e: A white cross on a red background is the Swiss cross. It is on many Swiss army knives.
77176.m: The Swiss cross is white on a red background.

77177.q: Which small tool on the Swiss army knife is meant?
77177.e: With a magnifying glass you see small things bigger. Some Swiss army knives have a small magnifying glass.
77177.m: A magnifying glass makes small things big.

77178.q: What are you doing here with the wood and the Swiss army knife?
77178.e: A duck is made from a piece of wood. Shaping wood with a knife is called whittling.
77178.m: When whittling you shape figures out of wood.

77179.q: Which vehicle runs on rails through the city here?
77179.e: A city, rails and a carriage show: the tram runs on rails through the streets of the city.
77179.m: The tram runs on rails right through the city.

77180.q: What is the train running on here?
77180.e: A train runs on rails. Two rails together are called a track.

77181.q: Which clock do these pictures mean?
77181.e: The clock hangs at the station. The Swiss railway station clock with its red second hand is very famous.
77181.m: The station clock has a red second hand.

77182.q: What do these pictures show together?
77182.e: For a train journey you need a ticket. Train and ticket make train ticket.
77182.m: You need a ticket for the train.

77183.q: What is the train going over here?
77183.e: Below the train there is a valley. The train is going over a bridge.

77184.q: What is the locomotive pulling here?
77184.e: Behind the locomotive there are three carriages. The engine pulls the carriages that people sit in.
77184.m: The locomotive pulls the carriages of the train.

77185.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
77185.e: A person is driving a train. This job is called train driver.
77185.m: The train driver drives the train.

77186.e: The train is leaving, and the person is running after it and is sad. He has missed the train.
77186.m: If you are too late, you miss the train.

77187.q: Which carriage on the train do these pictures mean?
77187.e: On the train you can eat and drink. This carriage is called the dining car.
77187.m: You can eat in the dining car.

77188.q: Which Swiss lake has a very tall water jet?
77188.e: In Lake Geneva the Jet d'eau shoots water about 140 metres high.
77188.m: The Jet d'eau is in Lake Geneva.

77189.q: Which city on Lake Lucerne do these pictures show?
77189.e: The wooden bridge with flowers and the tower is the Chapel Bridge with the Water Tower in Lucerne.
77189.m: The Chapel Bridge is in Lucerne.

77190.q: Which white bird is swimming on the lake here?
77190.e: The swan has a long neck and swims on many Swiss lakes.
77190.m: The swan has a long neck.

77191.q: What are people doing on the lake here?
77191.e: The person moves the boat forward with oars. That is rowing.
77191.m: When rowing you move the boat with oars.

77192.q: What are people using to cross the lake here?
77192.e: Large boats travel on many Swiss lakes. Some are old paddle steamers.
77192.m: Many boats travel on Swiss lakes.

77193.q: What are the children doing in the lake here in summer?
77193.e: In summer it is warm and you can swim in the lake.
77193.m: In summer you can swim in the lake.

77194.q: Which big lake lies between Switzerland, Germany and Austria?
77194.e: Three countries share one lake. That is Lake Constance.

77195.q: What is in the middle of the lake here?
77195.e: Land with water all round it is called an island. There are islands on Swiss lakes too.
77195.m: An island is completely surrounded by water.

77196.q: What happens here when it gets warmer?
77196.e: The thermometer shows warmth and the ice turns into water. That is why glaciers are getting smaller.
77196.m: When it gets warm, the ice melts.

77197.q: Which dangerous gap in a glacier is meant?
77197.e: In the ice of a glacier there are deep cracks. They are called crevasses and are dangerous.
77197.m: Crevasses are deep cracks in the ice.

77198.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77198.e: Ice and palace make ice palace. On the Jungfraujoch there is an ice palace inside the glacier.
77198.m: There is an ice palace on the Jungfraujoch.

77199.q: What is flowing from the glacier into the valley here?
77199.e: When the ice melts, water forms. This meltwater flows into the valley as a stream.
77199.m: Meltwater flows out of the glacier.

77200.q: What do you need on your boots on a glacier so that you do not slip?
77200.e: Crampons are metal spikes on your boots. They grip on the slippery ice.

77201.q: To which high place with a view of glaciers does this railway go?
77201.e: The Jungfrau Railway goes up through the mountain to the Jungfraujoch. From there you look out over huge glaciers.
77201.m: The Jungfrau Railway goes up to the Jungfraujoch.

77202.q: What is the biggest glacier in the Alps called?
77202.e: The medal shows first place. The Great Aletsch Glacier in Valais is the biggest glacier in the Alps.
77202.m: The Aletsch Glacier is the biggest glacier in the Alps.

77203.q: Which long cold period do these pictures show?
77203.e: The mammoth lived in the Ice Age. At that time almost all of Switzerland was covered by glaciers.
77203.m: In the Ice Age a lot of ice lay over Switzerland.

77204.q: Which famous building in Bern do these pictures show?
77204.e: The bear stands for Bern. The big building is the Federal Palace, where the government and parliament work.
77204.m: The government and parliament work in the Federal Palace in Bern.

77205.q: What are the people doing here?
77205.e: You fill in a slip of paper and put it in the ballot box. That is how people vote in Switzerland.
77205.m: In Switzerland the people often get to vote.

77206.q: Which group do these pictures mean?
77206.e: The number 7 is important. The Federal Council is the government of Switzerland and has seven members.
77206.m: The Federal Council has seven members.

77207.q: What is the big assembly in the Federal Palace that makes laws called?
77207.e: Lots of seats, a microphone and a speech: that is parliament. It makes the laws in the Federal Palace.

77208.q: What do the 26 water jets in front of the Federal Palace stand for?
77208.e: On the Federal Square there are 26 water jets. Each one stands for one of the 26 cantons.

77209.q: Which public holiday do these pictures mean?
77209.e: Fireworks, bonfires on the hills and paper lanterns belong to 1 August. That is Switzerland's national day.
77209.m: On 1 August Switzerland celebrates its birthday.

77210.q: What is the assembly called where people vote outdoors by raising their hands?
77210.e: At the Landsgemeinde people raise their hands outdoors. It still exists in the canton of Glarus and in Appenzell Innerrhoden.
77210.m: At the Landsgemeinde people vote by raising their hands.

77211.q: Which market in Bern do these pictures mean?
77211.e: Zibele means onions. At the Zibelemärit in November lots of onions are sold in Bern, including on the Federal Square.
77211.m: At the Zibelemärit in Bern there are lots of onions.

77212.q: What material is the alphorn made of?
77212.e: A tree and a piece of wood show the material. The alphorn is made of wood, often spruce.
77212.m: The alphorn is made of wood.

77213.q: Which singing from the mountains do these pictures mean?
77213.e: When yodelling, the voice switches quickly between high and low. Like the alphorn, yodelling is part of Swiss folk music.
77213.m: Yodelling is a way of singing from the mountains.

77214.q: Which Swiss instrument do these pictures show?
77214.e: The picture shows an accordion, and people are dancing. The Schwyzerörgeli is a small Swiss accordion.
77214.m: The Schwyzerörgeli is a Swiss accordion.

77215.q: What did herdsmen use the alphorn for in the past?
77215.e: The alphorn can be heard far away. In the past herdsmen used it to send signals across the valleys and call the cows.
77215.m: The alphorn can be heard a very long way off.

77216.q: Roughly how long is an alphorn?
77216.e: The ruler shows the length. An alphorn is usually about 3.5 metres long.
77216.m: An alphorn is longer than a car is wide.

77217.q: How do you make a note on the alphorn?
77217.e: You blow with your lips into the mouthpiece. That is how the notes are made.
77217.m: To play the alphorn you blow with your lips.

77218.q: Which job goes with these pictures?
77218.e: An instrument is built out of wood with tools. That is what an alphorn maker does.
77218.m: An alphorn maker builds alphorns out of wood.

77219.q: Which forest animal is digging its burrow here?
77219.e: The animal with the black and white striped head is the badger. It digs large burrows into the ground in the forest.
77219.m: The badger has a black and white striped head and lives in a burrow.

77220.q: Which mountain animal sleeps for a long time in its burrow in winter?
77220.e: The marmot lives in holes under the ground and hibernates for a long time.
77220.m: The marmot hibernates for a long time.

77222.q: Which large wild animal sometimes turns up in the Grisons?
77222.e: The bear in the forest and the tracks show the brown bear. Every now and then one wanders from Italy into the Grisons.
77222.m: Sometimes a brown bear comes into the Grisons.

77223.q: Which forest animal bellows loudly here in autumn?
77223.e: The animal with the large antlers is the stag. In autumn it bellows loudly in the forest.
77223.m: In autumn you can hear stags bellowing loudly in the forest.

77224.q: Which wild cat lives in Swiss forests?
77224.e: The brush shows the tufts of hair on the ears. The lynx has tufted ears like these and lives in the forest.
77224.m: The lynx has tufts on its ears.

77225.q: Which wild animal is looking for acorns in the forest here?
77225.e: The animal with bristly fur is a wild boar. With its snout it roots about in the forest floor for acorns.
77225.m: The wild boar roots in the forest floor for food with its snout.

77226.q: Which animal is warming itself on the stone here?
77226.e: The lizard lies on the warm stone in the sun. That is how it warms up its body.
77226.m: Lizards like to warm themselves on warm stones in the sun.
