78495.e: The red train runs over the spiral viaduct of Brusio down to Tirano in Italy in the south. At Ospizio Bernina the line reaches 2253 metres above sea level.
78495.m: The Bernina Express links the Grisons with Tirano in Italy.

78496.q: Which Swiss holiday resort does this picture puzzle make?
78496.e: The town lies between two lakes, Lake Thun and Lake Brienz. The Latin name “inter lacus” means “between the lakes”.
78496.m: The name Interlaken means “between the lakes”.

78497.q: Which destination do these emojis mean?
78497.e: The girl stands for “Jungfrau”, German for maiden, plus a mountain and a railway. Since 1912 the Jungfrau Railway has run to the highest railway station in Europe at 3454 metres.
78497.m: The Jungfraujoch is marketed as the “Top of Europe”.

78498.q: Which problem in tourism is meant?
78498.e: Too many visitors crowd around a sight, and the local people are fed up. This is called overtourism, known for example from Venice.
78498.m: Overtourism means a place is overloaded with too many tourists.

78499.q: Which form of tourism do these emojis show?
78499.e: Nature, hiking on foot and recycling stand for travel that puts as little strain as possible on the environment and local people.
78499.m: Sustainable tourism respects nature and local people.

78500.e: What is counted is the nights guests spend in beds in hotels and other accommodation. The Federal Statistical Office collects these overnight stays regularly.
78500.m: Overnight stays count how many nights guests stay.

78501.q: Which kind of holiday do these pictures mean?
78501.e: Guests stay on a farm, for example “sleeping in the straw”, and experience everyday life with animals. This kind of holiday is called agritourism.
78501.m: In agritourism you go on holiday on a farm.

78502.q: Which distinction do these emojis show?
78502.e: Buildings and landscapes of outstanding value for all of humanity are added to a list. In Switzerland, for example, the Abbey of St Gallen is on it.
78502.m: UNESCO World Heritage protects cultural and natural sites for all of humanity.

78503.e: The train travels through a 57-kilometre tunnel under the Alps. The Gotthard Base Tunnel opened in 2016 and is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
78503.m: At 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.

78504.q: Which form of transport do these emojis show?
78504.e: Whole lorries travelled through the Swiss Alps on railway wagons, so the road was rolling on the rails. This moved freight from road to rail; the service through Switzerland ended in December 2025.
78504.m: On the rolling motorway whole lorries travel by train.

78505.q: Which principle of rail transport is meant?
78505.e: Trains run regularly at the same minute, for example every hour. Switzerland introduced the nationwide regular-interval timetable in 1982.
78505.m: With a regular-interval timetable, trains run at fixed intervals.

78506.e: Anyone driving a car on Swiss motorways needs an annual sticker. The vignette costs 40 francs and is also available electronically.
78506.m: You may not drive on Swiss motorways without a vignette.

78507.q: Which charge do these emojis mean?
78507.e: The performance-related heavy vehicle charge depends on a lorry's weight and the kilometres it drives. It has been charged since 2001.
78507.m: The LSVA is calculated by weight, kilometres and emissions.

78508.q: Which type of traffic do these emojis show?
78508.e: Every day lots of people travel from home to work and back again. This regular journey to work is called commuter traffic.
78508.m: Commuters travel regularly between where they live and where they work.

78509.q: Which means of transport is meant?
78509.e: The ship carries standardised steel boxes, the containers. Such ships carry a large part of world trade; smaller container ships travel up the Rhine as far as Basel.
78509.m: Containers are standardised and easy to move between ship, train and lorry.

78510.q: Which mobility service do these emojis show?
78510.e: Bikes are shared, hired and returned using an app. This service is called bike sharing.
78510.m: With bike sharing you hire a bike for a short time using an app.

78511.e: The ticket divided by two makes half the price. With the Half Fare Travelcard, you travel on Swiss public transport at half price.
78511.m: With the Half Fare Travelcard, you pay only half price on public transport.

78512.e: The ship passes through locks, and the globe shows America. The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, links the Atlantic and the Pacific and lifts ships over the land with locks.
78512.m: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic with the Pacific.

78513.q: Which nickname of Switzerland is meant?
78513.e: Big rivers such as the Rhine, Rhône, Inn and Ticino rise in the Swiss Alps and flow into the North Sea, the Mediterranean, the Black Sea and the Adriatic. That is why Switzerland is called the water tower of Europe.
78513.m: Switzerland stores a lot of water for all of Europe in glaciers and lakes.

78514.q: Which body of water do these emojis show?
78514.e: The water is so salty that you can float on it while reading. The surface is about 430 metres below sea level, the lowest point on land.
78514.m: You can't sink in the Dead Sea because it is so salty.

78515.e: Red plus sea makes the Red Sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, which is known for its colourful coral reefs and fish.
78515.m: The Red Sea is famous for its coral reefs.

78517.q: Which sea do these emojis show?
78517.e: Olives, lemons and lots of sun typically grow and thrive around the Mediterranean Sea, which separates Europe, Africa and Asia.
78517.m: Around the Mediterranean, there is a warm climate with dry summers.

78518.q: Which ocean current does this picture puzzle make?
78518.e: Gulf plus stream makes Gulf Stream. The warm current comes from the Gulf of Mexico and gives Western Europe its mild climate.
78518.m: The Gulf Stream brings warm water to Europe.

78519.q: Which natural phenomenon do these emojis show?
78519.e: The pull of the Moon makes the sea level rise and fall regularly. This change between low tide and high tide is called the tides.
78519.m: Low and high tide are caused mainly by the pull of the Moon.

78520.q: Which climate zone do these emojis show?
78520.e: Palm trees, lots of rain and high temperatures all year round mark the tropics around the equator.
78520.m: In the tropics it is warm all year round.

78521.e: Penguins, snow and the polar night lasting for months mark the coldest areas of the Earth at the poles.
78521.m: In the polar zone, there is the polar night in winter.

78522.q: Which vegetation zone do these emojis show?
78522.e: Endless coniferous forests, long cold winters and elk or reindeer are typical of the taiga, the boreal coniferous forest in the north.
78522.m: The taiga is the largest forest area on Earth.

78523.e: Frozen ground, mosses and lichens instead of trees, and reindeer are typical of the tundra. The ground there is mostly frozen all year round.
78523.m: Hardly any trees grow in the tundra because of the cold.

78524.q: Which vegetation zone do these emojis show?
78524.e: Grassland with scattered trees, warmth and lions are typical of the savannah in the tropics with wet and dry seasons, for example in East Africa.
78524.m: In the savannah rainy and dry seasons alternate.

78525.q: Which climate zone do these pictures mean?
78525.e: Autumn, spring, summer and winter show the four clear seasons. They mark the temperate zone, where Switzerland lies too.
78525.m: Switzerland lies in the temperate climate zone.

78526.q: Which weather phenomenon do these emojis show?
78526.e: A wind that changes direction with the seasons and brings a rainy season is called a monsoon. It shapes the climate in India, for example.
78526.m: The monsoon brings the rainy season to South Asia every year.

78527.q: Which vegetation zone do these emojis show?
78527.e: Sand, dromedaries, cacti and strong sun mark the desert. So little rain falls there that hardly any plants grow.
78527.m: Very little rain falls in the desert.

78528.q: Which term from the business world is meant?
78528.e: A company hands a task over to another company, often abroad. Moving work out like this is called outsourcing.
78528.m: In outsourcing a company hands tasks over to other companies.

78529.q: Which term from competition law fits these pictures?
78529.e: Several companies secretly agree on their prices instead of competing with each other. Such an agreement is called a cartel; in Switzerland the Competition Commission COMCO takes action against it.
78529.m: A cartel is a banned agreement between companies, for example on prices.

78530.q: Which economic term is shown here?
78530.e: The inflated balloon stands for rising prices, and the money flying away for falling purchasing power. This process is called inflation (Latin inflare, to blow up).
78530.m: Inflation means that money loses purchasing power.

78531.q: Which investment strategy do these emojis show?
78531.e: The eggs are not all in the same basket but spread out. Anyone who spreads their money across different investments is diversifying and so lowers the risk.
78531.m: Diversification spreads the risk across several investments.

78532.q: Which term from the business world fits these pictures?
78532.e: Two companies shake hands and become one. Companies joining together is called a merger.
78532.m: In a merger companies join together.

78533.q: Which economic term do these emojis mean?
78533.e: A globe, a cargo ship, goods and connections stand for worldwide trade. The growing worldwide interconnection of the economy is called globalisation.

78534.q: Which market form do these pictures show?
78534.e: There is only one single supplier, who rules the market like a king. This market form is called a monopoly (Greek monos, alone).
78534.m: In a monopoly there is only one supplier.

78535.q: Which term from the world of shares is meant?
78535.e: Part of a company's profit is shared among the shareholders. This share of profit paid out is called a dividend (Latin dividere, to divide).
78535.m: The dividend is the share of profit that shareholders receive.

78536.q: Which term from politics and administration fits these pictures?
78536.e: Piles of files and forms in an office and a long wait stand for an administration with lots of rules. Bureaucracy literally means “rule of the desk” (French bureau).
78536.m: Bureaucracy means the administration and its fixed rules and procedures.

78537.q: Which political term fits these emojis?
78537.e: The raised hand and the no-entry sign in front of a decision stand for a right to object. The Latin word veto means “I forbid”.
78537.m: With a veto you can block a decision.

78538.q: Which form of government do these pictures show?
78538.e: The crown stands for a monarch, and the document and the scales for a constitution that limits his or her power. This is a constitutional monarchy, as in Sweden, for example.
78538.m: In a constitutional monarchy the monarch's power is limited by a constitution.

78539.q: Which form of rule do these emojis mean?
78539.e: The people decide on the institutions of the state. Democracy comes from the Greek demos (people) and kratein (to rule).
78539.m: Democracy means rule by the people.

78540.q: Which term from the Swiss parliament fits these pictures?
78540.e: Two parliament buildings stand for two chambers with equal rights. In Switzerland the National Council and the Council of States together form this two-chamber system.
78540.m: The Swiss parliament is a two-chamber system of the National Council and the Council of States.

78541.q: Which principle of the state do these jigsaw pieces show?
78541.e: Many independent parts fit together into one shared state. In federalism the member states, in Switzerland the cantons, keep their own responsibilities.
78541.m: Federalism divides power between the federal state and its member states.

78542.q: Which term from Swiss politics is meant?
78542.e: Different party colours shake hands. In Swiss concordance the big parties share the government, the Federal Council.
78542.m: Concordance means that the big parties govern together.

78543.q: Which political term fits these pictures?
78543.e: A person with a briefcase talks to politicians in the entrance hall of parliament. The English word lobby means entrance hall; lobbying is the attempt by interest groups to influence politics.
78543.m: In lobbying, interest groups try to influence politics.

78544.q: Which Latin legal principle is meant?
78544.e: If there is doubt, the verdict goes in favour of the accused. That is what In dubio pro reo means: “when in doubt, for the accused”.
78544.m: When in doubt, the court must decide in favour of the accused.

78545.q: Which legal principle fits these emojis?
78545.e: A contract and a handshake are kept. The Latin principle Pacta sunt servanda means “agreements must be kept”.
78545.m: Anyone who makes a contract must keep it.

78546.q: Which legal principle do these pictures mean?
a: No double punishment for the same act
When in doubt, for the accused
78546.e: The scales, the number 2 and the no-entry sign show: nobody may be convicted or punished twice for the same act. In Latin this principle is “Ne bis in idem”, not twice in the same matter.
78546.m: Nobody may be punished twice for the same act.

78547.q: Which term from criminal proceedings is meant?
78547.e: At the time of the crime the suspect was provably somewhere completely different. The Latin word alibi means “elsewhere”.
78547.m: An alibi proves that someone was elsewhere at the time of the crime.

78548.q: Which legal term fits these emojis?
78548.e: The door opens in return for money being deposited. With bail, a security payment, an accused person can be released until the trial.
78548.m: Bail is a sum of money deposited as security.

78549.q: Which term from the courtroom is meant?
78549.e: At the end of the hearing a speech is given in court. This final speech by the prosecution or the defence is called the closing speech, or plaidoyer.
78549.m: The closing speech is the final address in court.

78550.q: Which document from inheritance law do these emojis show?
78550.e: An older person writes down who should later receive the house and the money. This last wish is called a will.
78550.m: In a will you decide who inherits your property.

78551.e: An invention (light bulb) is protected by a certificate. A patent gives the right to use an invention exclusively for a maximum of 20 years.
78551.m: A patent protects an invention from being copied.

78552.q: Which medical term fits these pictures?
78552.e: A syringe builds a protective shield against germs. Building up protection like this, for example through a vaccination, is called immunisation.
78552.m: A vaccination produces immunisation against germs.

78553.q: Which technical term from hospital is meant?
78553.e: A patient sleeps so that they feel no pain during the operation. Switching off the sense of pain is called anaesthesia.
78553.m: Anaesthesia switches off the sense of pain.

78554.q: Which medical procedure do these emojis show?
78554.e: Blood is transferred from one person to another. This transfer of blood is called a transfusion (Latin transfundere, to pour across).
78554.m: In a transfusion a person receives someone else's blood.

78555.q: Which medical term do these pictures mean?
78555.e: An electric shock is given to the heart. In defibrillation this ends ventricular fibrillation so that the heart beats normally again.
78555.m: Defibrillation ends ventricular fibrillation with an electric shock.

78556.q: Which examination method do these emojis show?
78556.e: A small piece of tissue is cut out and examined under the microscope. This removal of tissue is called a biopsy.
78556.m: In a biopsy tissue is removed for examination.

78557.q: Which medical term fits these pictures?
78557.e: Brushing your teeth protects them before damage is done. Preventive measures are called prophylaxis.

78558.q: Which term from epidemiology is meant?
78558.e: A germ spreads across all continents. The worldwide spread of a disease is called a pandemic (Greek pan, all, and demos, people).
78558.m: A pandemic is the worldwide spread of a disease.

78559.q: Which medical term fits these emojis?
78559.e: Pollen makes you sneeze. An exaggerated defence reaction of the body to harmless substances such as pollen is called an allergy.
78559.m: With an allergy the body overreacts to harmless substances.

78560.q: Which effect from psychology is meant?
78560.e: A sugar pill with no active ingredient still leads to improvement because you believe it works. This is the placebo effect (Latin placebo, I shall please).
78560.m: In the placebo effect, simply believing in a treatment helps.

78561.q: Which error of perception do these emojis show?
78561.e: A halo makes a person seem good all round. In the halo effect one positive quality outshines the judgement of all the others.
78561.m: In the halo effect one feature colours the overall impression of a person.

78562.q: Which phenomenon from social psychology is meant?
78562.e: Lots of people watch an emergency, but nobody helps. In the bystander effect, people are less willing to help the more onlookers there are.
78562.m: The more onlookers there are, the less often someone helps.

78563.q: Which experience from psychology do these pictures show?
78563.e: You see something and feel you have experienced it exactly like this before. The French déjà vu means “already seen”.
78563.m: Déjà vu is the feeling of having experienced something before.

78564.q: Which phenomenon of perception is meant?
78564.e: Sounds are also perceived as colours. In synaesthesia two senses are linked (Greek syn, together, and aisthesis, perception).
78564.m: People with synaesthesia may, for example, perceive sounds as colours.

78565.q: Which ability do these emojis show?
78565.e: One person shares another's sadness with their heart. The ability to feel what others feel is called empathy.
78565.m: Empathy is the ability to put yourself in someone else's shoes.

78566.q: Which term from psychology fits these pictures?
78566.e: The homework is waiting and time is running out, but you are lying on the sofa with your phone. Constantly putting off tasks is called procrastination (Latin cras, tomorrow).
78566.m: Procrastination means putting off important tasks again and again.

78567.q: Which psychological quality do these emojis mean?
78567.e: The tree survives the storm and stays strong. Resilience is the ability to cope with crises and come out of them stronger.
78567.m: Resilient people get through crises better.

78568.q: Which term from psychology fits these pictures?
78568.e: A person is in love with their own reflection. Named after Narcissus from Greek legend, excessive self-love is called narcissism.
78568.m: Narcissism is an exaggerated love of yourself.

78569.q: Which technology do these emojis show?
78569.e: Sunlight is turned directly into electricity for the house. This technology with solar cells is called photovoltaics; solar thermal energy, by contrast, produces heat.
78569.m: Photovoltaics turns sunlight directly into electricity.

78570.q: Which form of energy do these pictures mean?
78570.e: Heat from inside the Earth rises and heats a house. Using the Earth's heat is called geothermal energy (Greek ge, earth, and thermos, warm).
78570.m: Geothermal energy uses the heat from inside the Earth.

78571.q: Which field of engineering fits these emojis?
78571.e: Large forces are transmitted using liquid, for example in a crane or an excavator. Transmitting force with liquids is called hydraulics (Greek hydor, water).

78572.q: Which field do these pictures mean?
78572.e: A robot with a mechanical arm works in a factory. The science of building and using robots is called robotics.

78573.q: Which technology do these emojis show?
78573.e: The computer receives a radio signal and needs no network cable. A wireless local network is called Wi-Fi or WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network).
78573.m: Wi-Fi connects devices to the network without cables.

78574.q: Which term from computing is meant?
78574.e: Data is stored not on the device but in a “cloud” on the internet and used from a laptop and a phone. This is called cloud computing.
78574.m: In cloud computing data and programs are kept on servers on the internet.

78575.q: Which technical term from computing fits these pictures?
78575.e: A set of instructions with clearly numbered steps is worked through by the computer. Such a precise set of instructions is called an algorithm, named after the scholar al-Khwarizmi.
78575.m: An algorithm is a step-by-step guide to solving a problem.

78576.q: Which term from product development is meant?
78576.e: A very first car is built by hand and tested. This first working model before mass production is called a prototype (Greek protos, first).
78576.m: A prototype is the first test model of a new product.

78577.q: Which musical performance marking do these emojis show?
78577.e: The loudspeaker goes from quiet to loud. Crescendo (Italian, growing) means that the music gradually gets louder.

78578.e: The volume goes down from loud to quiet. Decrescendo (Italian) means that the music gradually gets quieter.

78579.q: Which way of playing music do these pictures show?
78579.e: The notes are cut off and played short. Staccato (Italian, detached) means short and separated.
78579.m: Staccato notes are played short and separately.

78580.q: Which term from music do these emojis mean?
78580.e: Several people sing without a guitar or other instruments. Singing without instrumental accompaniment is called a cappella, “as in the chapel”.
78580.m: A cappella means singing without instruments.

78581.q: Which ensemble do these emojis show?
78581.e: Four string instruments play together. A string quartet consists of two violins, a viola and a cello.
78581.m: A string quartet consists of four string instruments.

78582.q: Which aid from music lessons is meant?
78582.e: A device gives a steady tempo while you play music. This device for keeping time is called a metronome.
78582.m: The metronome gives a steady tempo when you practise.

78583.q: Which tempo marking do these pictures show?
78583.e: The music slows down like a snail. Ritardando (Italian, delaying) means gradually getting slower.

78584.q: Which tempo marking do these emojis mean?
78584.e: The music picks up speed like a racing car. Accelerando (Italian, speeding up) means gradually getting faster.

78585.q: Which kind of picture do these emojis show?
78585.e: A painter looks in the mirror and paints himself. A picture like this is called a self-portrait; those by Rembrandt, for example, are famous.
78585.m: In a self-portrait, artists show themselves.

78586.q: Which genre of painting is meant?
78586.e: Fruit and a jug are painted as a still arrangement. A picture of lifeless objects is called a still life.
78586.m: A still life shows objects that don't move, such as fruit or vessels.

78587.q: Which painting technique do these pictures show?
78587.e: Paint is applied to a damp wall, often in churches. In a fresco (Italian fresco, fresh) you paint onto plaster that is still wet.
78587.m: A fresco is painted onto fresh, damp plaster.

78588.q: Which art technique do these emojis mean?
78588.e: Lots of small coloured squares together make a picture. In a mosaic, you put small stones or pieces of glass together to make a picture.
78588.m: A mosaic is made of lots of small coloured stones.

78589.q: Which painting technique goes with these emojis?
78589.e: Painting is done on paper with water, a brush and paint. Painting with see-through water-based paints is called watercolour (in German “Aquarell”, from Latin aqua, water).
78589.m: A watercolour is painted with water-based paints.

78590.q: Which art movement do these pictures mean?
78590.e: A sunrise and boats recall Claude Monet's painting “Impression, soleil levant” of 1872. Impressionism was named after this picture.
78590.m: Impressionism was named after a painting by Claude Monet.

78591.q: Which art movement do these emojis show?
78591.e: A face is put together from geometric shapes. In Cubism, Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque broke subjects down into cubes and flat surfaces.
78591.m: Cubism breaks subjects down into geometric shapes.

78592.q: Which art movement is meant here?
78592.e: Melting clocks and dream images recall Salvador Dalí's painting “The Persistence of Memory” of 1931. Surrealism shows dreamlike, unreal worlds.

78593.q: Which term from philosophy fits these pictures?
78593.e: A city where everyone lives happily is an ideal picture of society. The term utopia goes back to the book “Utopia” by Thomas More from 1516.
78593.m: A utopia describes an ideal but imaginary society.

78594.q: Which term do these emojis mean?
78594.e: A gloomy city with a watching eye and worried people shows a frightening future. Such a negative picture of the future is called a dystopia, as in George Orwell's “Nineteen Eighty-Four”.
78594.m: A dystopia describes a gloomy, threatening future.

78595.q: Which famous philosophical sentence is meant?
78595.e: Because someone is thinking, it is certain that they exist. René Descartes put this as Cogito, ergo sum, “I think, therefore I am”.
78595.m: Descartes concluded from his thinking that he exists.

78596.q: Which philosophical principle do these pictures show?
78596.e: Water keeps flowing, and everything changes over time. Panta rhei, “everything flows”, is attributed to the Greek philosopher Heraclitus.
78596.m: Panta rhei means that everything is constantly changing.

78597.q: Which term from the theory of knowledge is meant?
78597.e: A newborn baby is compared to an empty, freshly wiped slate. John Locke compared the mind at birth to a blank sheet; the term tabula rasa stands for this.

78598.q: Which philosophical teaching do these emojis show?
78598.e: Good food, parties and relaxing stand for enjoyment. Hedonism (Greek hedone, pleasure) sees pleasure and joy as the highest good.
78598.m: Hedonism sees enjoyment as the goal of life.

78599.q: Which school of philosophy do these pictures mean?
78599.e: A colonnade and a calm face in a thunderstorm: the Stoa was a colonnade in Athens. Stoicism teaches you to bear strokes of fate calmly.
78599.m: Stoicism teaches calm in the face of fate.

78600.e: People in a cave see only shadows that a fire casts on the wall. With this Allegory of the Cave, Plato described the path to knowledge.
78600.m: Plato's Allegory of the Cave is about shadows and true knowledge.

78601.q: Which principle of thinking do these emojis show?
78601.e: A razor cuts everything unnecessary away from an idea. According to Occam's razor, the simplest of several explanations should be preferred.
78601.m: Occam's razor advises choosing the simplest explanation.

78602.q: Which term from sport is meant?
78602.e: Three goals and a hat: in football a player scores a hat-trick by scoring three goals in one match. The term comes from cricket, where a hat was once given for it.
78602.m: In a hat-trick a player scores three goals in one match.

78603.q: Which term from athletics fits these pictures?
78603.e: Two runners reach the finish almost at the same time, and a camera decides. Deciding the finish by photo is called a photo finish.
78603.m: In a photo finish a photo of the finish line decides who wins.

78604.q: Which term from cycling is meant?
78604.e: A cyclist rides close behind another and is sheltered from the wind. Riding in someone's slipstream saves a lot of energy.
78604.m: In the slipstream you ride with less effort.

78605.q: Which tennis term do these emojis show?
78605.e: When a set reaches 6 games all, a special deciding game is usually played. This game is called a tiebreak.
78605.m: A tiebreak decides a set at 6 games all.

78606.q: Which running event do these pictures mean?
78606.e: The number 42 stands for the distance of 42.195 kilometres. This long-distance race is called a marathon, named after the Greek town of Marathon.

78607.q: Which sport do these emojis show?
78607.e: Swimming, cycling and running are done straight after each other. This endurance sport is called triathlon (Greek tri, three).
78607.m: The triathlon is made up of swimming, cycling and running.

78608.q: Which winter sport do these pictures stand for?
78608.e: Skiing and a target stand for the combination of cross-country skiing and shooting. This winter sport is called biathlon (Greek bi, two).
78608.m: Biathlon combines cross-country skiing with shooting at targets.

78609.e: A ball lies about 11 metres in front of the goal, and only the goalkeeper may try to stop it. This kick is called a penalty.
78609.m: A penalty is taken from the penalty spot.

78613.q: Which linguistic term do these emojis show?
78613.e: Hot and cold are opposites. A word with the opposite meaning is called an antonym.
78613.m: An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning.

78614.q: Which figure of speech do these pictures stand for?
78614.e: The cat says “miaow”, and the word imitates the sound. This sound painting is called onomatopoeia.

78615.q: Which figure of speech do these emojis show?
78615.e: The sun smiles and waves like a person. When things or natural phenomena are given human qualities, this is called personification.
78615.m: In personification, things are given human qualities.

78616.e: In the telling, a tiny ant turns into a gigantic dinosaur, so something is greatly exaggerated. Strong exaggeration is called hyperbole.
78616.m: A hyperbole is a strong exaggeration.

78617.q: Which figure of speech do these pictures show when you name them in English?
78617.e: Bee, banana and bread all begin with the same sound B. The same initial sound in words that follow each other is called alliteration.
78617.m: In alliteration, words begin with the same sound.

78618.q: Which figure of speech do these emojis stand for?
78618.e: In rainy weather someone says grumpily “Great weather!”. When you say the opposite of what you mean, that is irony.
78618.m: Irony means the opposite of what is said.

78619.q: Which word borrowed from French do these emojis stand for?
78619.e: From a trip to Paris you bring a small keepsake home in your suitcase. The French word souvenir means “memory”.
78619.m: A souvenir is a keepsake from a trip.

78620.q: Which Latin expression fits these pictures?
78620.e: A document goes into the folder and into the archive, the matter is closed. To put something “ad acta” literally means “to the files”, so to regard it as finished.
78620.m: If you put something ad acta, you regard the matter as finished.

78622.q: Which job with a French name goes with these emojis?
78622.e: A person with a cap drives other people in a car. Someone who drives a vehicle as a job is called a chauffeur.
78622.m: A chauffeur drives other people in a car.

78623.q: Which job with a French name is meant?
78623.e: Hair is cut with scissors, and the striped sign stands for a salon. In Switzerland, a hairdresser is called a coiffeur.
78623.m: The coiffeur cuts and styles hair.

78624.q: Which word borrowed from French fits these pictures?
78624.e: A wrong step leads to an embarrassing moment. Faux pas means “false step” in French and refers to a breach of good manners.
78624.m: A faux pas is an embarrassing breach of good manners.

78625.q: Which word borrowed from French is meant?
78625.e: Two people meet with a rose at a set time at a set place. Such an arranged meeting is called a rendezvous.
78625.m: A rendezvous is an arranged meeting.

78626.q: Which loanword from the art world fits these emojis?
78626.e: An exhibition of paintings opens its doors with a party. The festive opening of an art exhibition is called a vernissage.
78626.m: The vernissage is the opening of an exhibition.

78628.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
a: Renoir’s “Bal du moulin de la Galette”
78628.e: In 1888 in Arles, Vincent van Gogh painted several pictures of sunflowers in a vase, all in bright yellow.
78628.m: Van Gogh painted his sunflowers in a vase and almost only in shades of yellow.

78629.q: Which famous painting do these pictures stand for?
78629.e: Van Gogh’s “Starry Night” (1889) shows a swirling night sky with stars and the moon above a village with a church tower.
78629.m: The swirling spirals in the sky make Van Gogh’s “Starry Night” unmistakable.

78630.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
78630.e: In 1893 Edvard Munch painted a desperate figure on a bridge under a glowing orange-red sky above the Oslofjord.
78630.m: Munch’s “The Scream” is seen as a symbol of the anxiety of modern people.

78631.q: Which painting do these emojis mean?
78631.e: Leonardo da Vinci painted the woman with the mysterious smile in front of a wide landscape; the picture hangs today in the Louvre in Paris.
78631.m: The Mona Lisa's smile is seen as the most famous in the history of art.

78632.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
78632.e: Around 1665, Jan Vermeer painted a girl with a blue and yellow turban and a large pearl at her ear; the shell stands for the pearl.
78632.m: Vermeer’s girl wears a blue and yellow turban and a large pearl.

78633.q: Which work of art do these pictures stand for?
78633.e: Around 1830, Katsushika Hokusai created a woodblock print with a huge wave threatening boats and Mount Fuji in the background.
78633.m: Hokusai’s “Great Wave” is the best-known Japanese woodblock print.

78634.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
78634.e: In 1931 Salvador Dalí painted soft, melting pocket watches in a bare coastal landscape; ants are crawling on one watch.
78634.m: Dalí’s melting clocks are among the best-known images of the 20th century.

78635.q: Which painting do these emojis stand for?
78635.e: In 1964 René Magritte painted a man in a bowler hat and suit whose face is hidden by a floating green apple, in front of a cloudy sky.
78635.m: Magritte hid the face of his man in a bowler hat behind an apple.

78636.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
a: “A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte”
78636.e: In 1942 Edward Hopper painted lonely customers at night in a brightly lit diner behind a large pane of glass.
78636.m: Hopper’s “Nighthawks” shows loneliness in the big city at night.

78637.q: Which building do these emojis stand for?
78637.e: The free-standing bell tower of Pisa Cathedral was built from 1173 and already began to lean during construction; the pizza stands for Italy.
78637.m: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral.

78638.q: Which structure do these emojis stand for?
78638.e: The covered wooden bridge in Lucerne has triangular painted panels in its gables; in 1993 most of it burned down and it was then rebuilt.
78638.m: Lucerne’s Chapel Bridge is considered the oldest surviving medieval wooden bridge in Europe.

78639.q: Which building do these emojis stand for?
78639.e: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had the white marble tomb built on the Yamuna river in Agra for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal.
78639.m: The Taj Mahal is a white marble tomb and a symbol of love.

78640.q: Which site do these emojis show?
78640.e: The Incas built the city around 1450 high in the Andes of Peru; in 1911 an expedition led by Hiram Bingham made it world-famous. The llama stands for the Andes.
78640.m: Machu Picchu is an Inca city high in the Andes of Peru.

78641.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
78641.e: The fountain in Lake Geneva shoots water about 140 metres into the air and is the landmark of Geneva.
78641.m: The Jet d’eau is the landmark of Geneva.

78642.q: Which building do these emojis show?
78642.e: The Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens was dedicated to the goddess Athena, whose animal and plant are the owl and the olive tree.
78642.m: The Parthenon on the Acropolis was the temple of the goddess Athena.

78643.q: Which building do these emojis stand for?
78643.e: The round fortress above Schaffhausen was built from 1564 to 1589; vines grow on its slope, and every evening at 9 pm the Munot watchwoman rings the little Munot bell.
78643.m: The Munot is the round fortress of Schaffhausen.

78644.q: Which building do these emojis show?
78644.e: Cologne Cathedral with its two tall towers was built from 1248 to 1880, with long breaks, so over 632 years.
78644.m: Building Cologne Cathedral took over 600 years.

78645.q: Which structure do these emojis show?
78645.e: The 285-metre-high dam in Valais holds back the Lac des Dix; it is the highest gravity dam in the world and the tallest structure in Switzerland.
78645.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest gravity dam in the world.

78646.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
78646.e: Antonio Vivaldi wrote four violin concertos that portray spring, summer, autumn and winter in music.
78646.m: Vivaldi’s “Four Seasons” are four violin concertos.

78647.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78647.e: In 1717 George Frideric Handel had his “Water Music” played on boats on the Thames for King George I.
78647.m: Handel’s “Water Music” was played in 1717 during the king’s boat trip on the Thames.

78648.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
a: “In the Hall of the Mountain King”
78648.e: Edvard Grieg wrote the piece for Ibsen’s “Peer Gynt”: Peer ends up among the trolls of the Mountain King, and the music gets faster and louder.
78648.m: In Grieg’s “Hall of the Mountain King” the music keeps getting faster and louder.

78649.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78649.e: In his suite of 1886, Camille Saint-Saëns portrays lions, elephants, tortoises, kangaroos and other animals in music.
78649.m: In “The Carnival of the Animals” every animal has its own music.

78650.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
78650.e: In Sergei Prokofiev’s musical fairy tale (1936) each character stands for an instrument: Peter, the wolf, the duck, the bird and the cat.
78650.m: In “Peter and the Wolf” you get to know the instruments of the orchestra.

78651.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78651.e: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov wrote “Flight of the Bumblebee” for his opera “The Tale of Tsar Saltan” (1900); the racing runs of the violin imitate the buzzing.
78651.m: Rimsky-Korsakov’s “Flight of the Bumblebee” imitates a bumblebee’s buzzing with racing notes.

78652.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
78652.e: In Maurice Ravel’s “Boléro” (1928) the snare drum plays the same rhythm throughout the whole piece, while the music gets louder and louder.
78652.m: Ravel’s “Boléro” repeats one rhythm and keeps getting louder.

78653.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78653.e: The four opening notes of Beethoven’s 5th Symphony are often interpreted as “Thus fate knocks at the door”; hence the name Symphony of Fate.
78653.m: Beethoven’s Fifth begins with four famous notes like a knock at the door.

78654.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78654.e: In Mozart’s opera (1791) magic instruments help; the bird catcher Papageno appears, and Tamino flees from a serpent and searches for Princess Pamina.
78654.m: Mozart’s “Magic Flute” tells of the bird catcher Papageno and Prince Tamino.

78655.q: Which opera do these emojis show?
78655.e: Georges Bizet’s opera (1875) is set in Seville, the city of oranges; Carmen dances, throws a flower and falls in love with a bullfighter.
78655.m: Bizet’s “Carmen” is set in Seville and contains the famous Toreador Song.

78656.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78656.e: Giuseppe Verdi’s opera (1871) is set in ancient Egypt; the Ethiopian princess Aida lives as a captive, and the Triumphal March with trumpets is famous.
78656.m: Verdi’s “Aida” is set in ancient Egypt and is known for its Triumphal March.

78657.q: Which opera do these emojis show?
78657.e: In Giacomo Puccini’s opera, the Chinese princess Turandot sets every suitor three riddles.
78657.m: Princess Turandot sets her suitors three riddles.

78658.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78658.e: In Puccini’s opera (1904) the Japanese woman Cio-Cio-San, called Butterfly, waits in Nagasaki for her American naval officer to return.
78658.m: “Madama Butterfly” is set in Nagasaki and tells of a sad love story.

78659.q: Which operatic work do these emojis show?
78659.e: Richard Wagner’s four-part work begins with three Rhinemaidens guarding the Rhinegold, from which a ring is forged; at the end there is a great fire that destroys the world.
78659.m: Wagner’s “Ring of the Nibelung” consists of four operas.

78660.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78660.e: In Wagner’s opera a knight arrives in a boat drawn by a swan; he marries Elsa (Bridal Chorus), but she must never ask his name.
78660.m: In Wagner’s opera, Lohengrin is the mysterious Swan Knight.

78661.q: Which opera do these emojis show?
78661.e: In Wagner’s opera (1843) a cursed captain must sail the seas for ever with his ghost ship.
78661.m: The Flying Dutchman is a captain who sails the seas without rest.

78662.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78662.e: In the musical with the songs of ABBA, Sophie invites three men to her wedding on a Greek island, because one of them could be her father. It premiered in London in 1999.
78662.m: “Mamma Mia!” tells a story with the songs of ABBA.

78663.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78663.e: Andrew Lloyd Webber’s “Cats” is set on a full-moon night in a scrapyard where the cats gather; it is based on poems by T. S. Eliot.
78663.m: In “Cats” the cats meet at night in a scrapyard.

78664.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78664.e: A masked musician lives beneath the Paris Opera, plays the organ and rows his singer Christine across an underground lake full of candles.
78664.m: The Phantom of the Opera wears a mask and lives beneath the Paris opera house.

78665.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78665.e: “Wicked” tells the story of the green-skinned witch Elphaba from the Land of Oz, who flies on a broomstick and travels to the Emerald City.
78665.m: “Wicked” tells the story of the witches of Oz before the famous tale.

78666.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78666.e: Jean Valjean was in a prison camp for stealing bread, is given silver candlesticks by the bishop and later takes care of the girl Cosette.
78666.m: “Les Misérables” is based on the novel by Victor Hugo.

78667.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78667.e: The nanny Mary Poppins arrives with the east wind, flying on her umbrella, pulls everything out of her bag and sings about a spoonful of sugar.
78667.m: Mary Poppins floats through the air with her umbrella.

78668.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78668.e: Near Salzburg, young Maria becomes the governess of the seven von Trapp children and teaches them to sing with her guitar.
78668.m: “The Sound of Music” tells of Maria and the von Trapp family.

78669.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78669.e: In “Starlight Express” the performers race each other on roller skates as locomotives and carriages; it has been running in Bochum since 1988.
78669.m: In “Starlight Express” the performers move on roller skates.

78670.q: Which group of artists do these emojis stand for?
78670.e: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner and other architecture students founded the Expressionist group “Die Brücke” (The Bridge) in Dresden in 1905.
78670.m: The artists’ group “Die Brücke” was founded in Dresden in 1905.

78671.q: Which art movement do these emojis show?
78671.e: Futurism, proclaimed by Filippo Tommaso Marinetti in 1909, celebrated speed, machines and modern technology.
78671.m: Futurism was fascinated by speed and machines.

78672.q: Which art movement do these emojis stand for?
78672.e: Art Nouveau around 1900 loved curving lines modelled on plants, flowers and peacocks.
78672.m: Art Nouveau decorates with curving plant shapes.

78673.q: Which art movement do these emojis show?
78673.e: Dada began in 1916 at the Cabaret Voltaire in Zurich; the name sounds like baby talk and means hobby horse in French, and collages and sound poems are typical.
78673.m: Dada was founded in Zurich in 1916.

78674.q: Which art movement do these emojis stand for?
78674.e: Andy Warhol painted soup cans, Roy Lichtenstein enlarged comic pictures with speech bubbles; both stand for Pop Art.
78674.m: Pop Art turned everyday objects and comics into art.

78675.q: Which period of art do these emojis show?
78675.e: Renaissance means rebirth: antiquity was rediscovered, and artists used the newly studied central perspective.
78675.m: In the Renaissance the art of antiquity was reborn.

78676.q: Which period of art do these emojis stand for?
78676.e: Rococo is named after rocaille, a shell-shaped ornament; playful curves and delicate pastel colours are typical.
78676.m: Rococo takes its name from a shell ornament.

78677.q: Which group of artists do these emojis show?
78677.e: Wassily Kandinsky and Franz Marc founded the group “Der Blaue Reiter” (The Blue Rider) in Munich in 1911; Marc often painted blue horses.
78677.m: Franz Marc and Wassily Kandinsky founded the Blue Rider.

78678.q: Which architectural style do these emojis stand for?
78678.e: Gothic cathedrals rise high with pointed arches and have huge coloured stained-glass windows.
78678.m: Gothic architecture built tall churches with pointed arches and colourful stained glass.

78679.q: Which school of architecture and design do these emojis show?
78679.e: The Bauhaus was founded by Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919; the name is made of the German words for building and house, and basic shapes and primary colours are typical.
78679.m: The Bauhaus combined art, craft and architecture.

78680.q: Which architect do these emojis stand for?
78680.e: Le Corbusier from La Chaux-de-Fonds developed the Modulor system of measurement based on the human body and appeared on the Swiss ten-franc note of the 8th series.
78680.m: Le Corbusier came from La Chaux-de-Fonds and invented the Modulor.

78681.q: Which architect do these emojis stand for?
78681.e: Gaudí’s basilica Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882; his colourful mosaic lizard is in Park Güell.
78681.m: Gaudí’s Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been a building site for over a hundred years.

78682.q: Which artist and architect do these emojis stand for?
78682.e: Hundred and water make Hundertwasser (German hundert and Wasser); his houses are colourful and crooked, with trees planted on the roofs and in the windows.
78682.m: Hundertwasser loved colourful façades and trees on the roofs.

78683.q: Which order of columns do these emojis stand for?
78683.e: The Ionic capital has two spiral volutes that look like ram’s horns.
78683.m: You can recognise Ionic columns by the rolled spirals on the capital.

78684.q: Which order of columns do these emojis show?
78684.e: According to Vitruvius, the Corinthian capital was inspired by a basket around which acanthus leaves grew; hence its rings of leaves.
78684.m: Corinthian columns have a capital of acanthus leaves.

78685.q: Which structure do these emojis stand for?
78685.e: In 1989 the architect I. M. Pei built the glass pyramid as the entrance to the Louvre art museum in Paris.
78685.m: The glass pyramid is the entrance to the Louvre in Paris.

78686.q: Which typeface do these emojis stand for?
78686.e: Helvetica was designed in Switzerland in 1957; its name comes from the Latin Helvetia for Switzerland.
78686.m: Helvetica is a world-famous typeface from Switzerland.

78687.q: Which design object do these emojis show?
78687.e: Hans Hilfiker designed the Swiss railway clock in 1944; later the red second hand shaped like a signal paddle was added.
78687.m: The Swiss railway clock has a red second hand like a signal paddle.

78688.q: Which design classic do these emojis stand for?
78688.e: Hans Coray designed the aluminium chair with a perforated seat for the Swiss National Exhibition of 1939, the Landi.
78688.m: The aluminium Landi chair was designed for the 1939 National Exhibition.

78689.q: Which design classic do these emojis show?
78689.e: Verner Panton designed the first chair made from a single piece of plastic, curved in an S shape and often red.
78689.m: The Panton Chair is made from a single piece of plastic.

78690.q: Which art and design movement do these emojis stand for?
78690.e: From 1917, Piet Mondrian and the De Stijl group worked only with straight black lines, white and the primary colours red, blue and yellow.
78690.m: De Stijl limited itself to straight lines and primary colours.

78691.q: Which design principle do these emojis show?
78691.e: The spiral of a snail shell is often linked to the golden ratio, a ratio of about 1 to 1.618 that is seen as especially harmonious.
78691.m: The golden ratio is seen as an especially harmonious proportion.

78692.q: Which colour relationship do these emojis stand for?
78692.e: Red and green, and blue and orange, lie opposite each other on the colour wheel and intensify each other.
78692.m: Complementary colours lie opposite each other on the colour wheel.

78693.q: Which typography term do these emojis show?
78693.e: Serifs are the small feet at the ends of letters, as in Times New Roman.
78693.m: Serifs are the small feet on letters.

78694.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78694.e: Prince Hamlet of the Danish castle of Elsinore ponders life in the soliloquy “To be or not to be” and holds the skull of the jester Yorick in the graveyard.
78694.m: Shakespeare’s Hamlet asks the famous question “To be or not to be”.

78695.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78695.e: In the famous balcony scene Romeo speaks at night beneath Juliet’s window; the rose recalls her line about names.
78695.m: The balcony scene is the most famous scene from “Romeo and Juliet”.

78696.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78696.e: In Shakespeare’s comedy, fairies play tricks in the woods at night; a craftsman is given a donkey’s head, and Titania, under a spell, falls in love with him.
78696.m: In “A Midsummer Night’s Dream” fairies enchant people in the woods at night.

78697.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78697.e: In Lessing’s drama (1779) the wise Nathan tells the parable of the three identical rings and pleads for tolerance between religions.
78697.m: Lessing’s ring parable pleads for tolerance between religions.

78698.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78698.e: In Goethe’s drama the scholar Faust makes a pact with the devil Mephisto, who first appears as a poodle (“so that was the poodle’s core!”).
78698.m: Goethe’s “Faust” is the best-known drama in German literature.

78699.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78699.e: In Friedrich Dürrenmatt’s play (1956) an old billionairess arrives by train in her impoverished home village of Güllen and offers money on a terrible condition.
78699.m: Dürrenmatt’s “The Visit” shows how money corrupts the morals of a community.

78700.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78700.e: In Dürrenmatt’s comedy (1962) three physicists live in a mental asylum; one of them wants to hide dangerous formulas from the world.
78700.m: Dürrenmatt’s “The Physicists” is about the responsibility of science.

78701.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78701.e: In Max Frisch’s play (1958) Mr Biedermann takes two strangers into his house, even though they store drums of petrol in his attic.
78701.m: Max Frisch’s “The Fire Raisers” warns against blindly looking away.

78702.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78702.e: In Samuel Beckett’s play two men wait in vain by a bare tree for someone who never comes.
78702.m: In “Waiting for Godot” they wait for someone who never turns up.

78703.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78703.e: Claude Nobs founded the jazz festival on the shore of Lake Geneva in Montreux in 1967.
78703.m: The Montreux Jazz Festival has taken place on Lake Geneva since 1967.

78704.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78704.e: The Gurtenfestival takes place on the Gurten, Bern’s local mountain; the bear stands for Bern.
78704.m: The Gurtenfestival takes place on Bern’s local mountain.

78705.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78705.e: Since 1992, Love Mobiles with techno music have been driving around the lake basin in Zurich at the Street Parade; often around 900,000 visitors come.
78705.m: The Street Parade is a huge techno party on Lake Zurich.

78706.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78706.e: The Berlinale takes place every February; the main prize is the Golden Bear.
78706.m: At the Berlinale the best film wins the Golden Bear.

78707.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78707.e: At the film festival on the Côte d’Azur the main prize awarded is the Palme d’Or (Golden Palm).
78707.m: In Cannes the best film wins the Palme d’Or.

78708.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78708.e: The Venice Film Festival (since 1932) is the oldest in the world; the main prize is the Golden Lion, and the gondola stands for Venice.
78708.m: In Venice the best film wins the Golden Lion.

78709.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78709.e: The Lucerne Festival brings classical orchestras to Lucerne, the city of the Lion Monument on Lake Lucerne.
78709.m: The Lucerne Festival is one of the most important festivals of classical music.

78710.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78710.e: At the Salzburg Festival, Hofmannsthal’s “Jedermann” (Everyman), a play about a rich man and death, has been performed in front of the cathedral since 1920.
78710.m: “Jedermann” has been performed in front of Salzburg Cathedral every summer since 1920.

78711.q: Which Swiss painter do these emojis stand for?
78711.e: Around 1910 Ferdinand Hodler painted “The Woodcutter”; from 1911 the image appeared on the Swiss 50-franc note.
78711.m: Hodler’s “Woodcutter” could be seen on the 50-franc note for decades.

78712.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78712.e: Alberto Giacometti created long, thin figures such as “Walking Man”; he appeared on the 100-franc note of the 8th series.
78712.m: Giacometti is famous for his thin, elongated bronze figures.

78713.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78713.e: Jean Tinguely built moving machine sculptures from cogwheels and scrap; in Basel his figures spray water in the Tinguely Fountain.
78713.m: Tinguely built machines that move and make noise.

78714.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78714.e: In 1936 Meret Oppenheim covered a cup, saucer and spoon with gazelle fur; the object “Breakfast in Fur” made her world-famous.
78714.m: Meret Oppenheim became world-famous with her fur-covered cup.

78715.q: Which artist do these emojis stand for?
78715.e: The clover leaf stands for the name Klee (German for clover); in 1925 Paul Klee painted the picture “The Goldfish”. The Zentrum Paul Klee is in Bern.
78715.m: Paul Klee grew up in Bern, where the Zentrum Paul Klee stands today.

78716.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78716.e: Sophie Taeuber-Arp from Davos danced with the Dadaists, taught textile design and created pictures of triangles, circles and rectangles; she was on the 50-franc note of the 8th series.
78716.m: Sophie Taeuber-Arp was a dancer, textile artist and painter of geometric pictures.

78717.q: Which painter do these emojis stand for?
78717.e: Giovanni Segantini painted the Engadine in the bright mountain sunlight; his Alpine triptych “Life, Nature, Death” hangs in the Segantini Museum in St Moritz.
78717.m: Segantini’s Alpine triptych can be seen in the Segantini Museum in St Moritz.

78718.q: Which song do these emojis stand for?
78718.e: In 1841 Alberich Zwyssig set to music the text by Leonhard Widmer, which begins with the red dawn; since 1981 the Swiss Psalm has officially been the national anthem of Switzerland.
78718.m: The Swiss Psalm has been Switzerland’s official national anthem since 1981.

78719.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78719.e: Basel Carnival begins at 4 am with the Morgestraich: the lights go out, and groups called cliques march through the city with drums and lanterns.
78719.m: The Morgestraich at 4 am opens Basel Carnival.

78720.q: Which Swiss festival do these emojis show?
78720.e: The winegrowers’ festival in Vevey takes place only about every 20 to 25 years, most recently in 2019 in an arena with 20,000 seats; since 2016 it has been UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.
78720.m: The Fête des Vignerons in Vevey is celebrated only about once a generation.

78721.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78721.e: In Liestal, on the Sunday of carnival, burning bundles of wood (Chienbäse) and fire wagons are carried and pulled through the old town at night.
78721.m: At Chienbäse, burning wagons are pulled through the town gate in Liestal.

78722.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78722.e: In January in Basel, the Wild Man travels down the Rhine on a raft with a small fir tree; with the griffin (Vogel Gryff) and the lion he dances through Kleinbasel.
78722.m: At Vogel Gryff the griffin, the lion and the Wild Man dance through Kleinbasel.

78723.q: Which Swiss tradition do these emojis stand for?
78723.e: In Hornussen the puck (Nouss) is hit far across a field and buzzes like a hornet; the opponents stop it with wooden boards.
78723.m: In Hornussen the team stops the Nouss with wooden boards.

78724.q: Which Swiss tradition do these emojis show?
78724.e: In stone throwing, the Unspunnen stone, which weighs about 83.5 kilograms, is thrown as far as possible.
78724.m: The Unspunnen stone weighs about 83.5 kilograms.

78725.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78725.e: At the Eierläset after Easter, runners collect raw eggs from little piles of sawdust and throw them to a catcher with a big basket; the faster team wins.
78725.m: At the Eierläset, spring beats winter in a race with raw eggs.

78726.q: Which Swiss tradition do these emojis show?
78726.e: In the Justistal near Sigriswil, the summer’s alpine cheese is shared out in September: each farmer gets as much cheese as his cows gave milk.
78726.m: At the Chästeilet, the alpine cheese is shared out according to how much milk the cows gave.

78727.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78727.e: In Appenzell Ausserrhoden, on 31 December and 13 January, the “beautiful”, the “ugly” and the “beautiful-ugly” Chläuse go from farm to farm with bells and large headdresses.
78727.m: The Silvesterchläuse walk through the Appenzell region with bells and headdresses.

78728.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78728.e: Price tags and two falling curves show that prices in the shops are generally going down. A lasting fall in the price level is called deflation.
78728.m: In deflation, the general price level falls over a longer period.

78729.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78729.e: The factory with a falling curve and the worker with a cross stand for shrinking production and job cuts. When economic output shrinks over several quarters, it is called a recession.
78729.m: In a recession, economic output shrinks and jobs are lost.

78730.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78730.e: The goods (parcel) and the customers (raised hand) are on the two sides of a pair of scales. How supply and demand balance out determines the price in a free market.
78730.m: In a free market, supply and demand determine the price.

78731.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78731.e: Three workers each do a different task: screwing, painting, packing. Splitting work into separate steps like this is called division of labour; Adam Smith described it in 1776 using the example of pin making.
78731.m: With division of labour, each person specialises in one step.

78732.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78732.e: A coin, shopping bags and a muscle stand for money, buying and power. Purchasing power tells you how many goods you can buy with a certain amount of money.
78732.m: Purchasing power shows how much you can afford with your money.

78733.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78733.e: The factory and the curves that rise and fall in turn, with the circular arrow, show a recurring up and down. This regular rise and fall of the economy is called the business cycle.
78733.m: The business cycle describes the recurring ups and downs of the economy.

78734.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78734.e: Money flows from the state (government building) to a farm (tractor). Financial support like this from the state, without anything given directly in return, is called a subsidy.
78734.m: A subsidy is state money to help particular businesses or industries.

78735.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78735.e: An idea (light bulb), a rocket and an office building stand for a new company that wants to grow fast with an innovative idea. Young companies like this are called start-ups.
78735.m: A start-up is a young company with a new business idea.

78736.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78736.e: Parliament passes a law, the people raise their hands, collect signatures and vote. In Switzerland an optional referendum needs 50,000 signatures within 100 days.
78736.m: With a referendum, the people can vote on a law passed by parliament.

78737.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78737.e: A signed letter is sent by post to an authority. In Switzerland anyone may send a request or suggestion to the authorities with a petition (Art. 33 of the Federal Constitution).
78737.m: A petition is a written request to an authority that anyone may submit.

78738.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78738.e: A red party and a blue party shake hands in parliament. Such an alliance of several parties, usually to govern together, is called a coalition.
78738.m: A coalition is an alliance of parties that govern together.

78739.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78739.e: The ballot box, the finger on the lips and the lock show that nobody may find out how someone votes. The secret ballot protects free voting.
78739.m: The secret ballot guarantees that nobody finds out how you voted.

78740.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78740.e: A megaphone and a newspaper spread lies that are meant to get into people’s heads. Propaganda is the deliberate, often one-sided or false influencing of many people’s opinions.
78740.m: Propaganda tries to influence people’s opinions deliberately and one-sidedly.

78741.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78741.e: Something is cut out of a newspaper and banned. When the state suppresses content before or after publication, it is called censorship; the Federal Constitution forbids it (Art. 17).
78741.m: Censorship means that content is suppressed or banned.

78742.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78742.e: The ballot box and the boxing glove together stand for an election and a fight. In an election campaign, parties and candidates compete for votes before an election.
78742.m: In an election campaign, parties compete for people’s votes before an election.

78743.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78743.e: A newspaper, an open lock, a fountain pen and a microphone stand for media that may report freely. Freedom of the press (in Switzerland called media freedom) is a fundamental right.
78743.m: Thanks to freedom of the press, the media may report independently.

78744.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78744.e: Whoever writes (hand with pen) creates a work like a book; the copyright symbol and the scales stand for legal protection. In Switzerland copyright usually protects works until 70 years after the author’s death.
78744.m: Copyright protects creative works such as books, music and pictures.

78745.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78745.e: In court (scales) a person counts as innocent (angel face) as long as their guilt has not been proven (question mark, magnifying glass). This principle is called the presumption of innocence and is in Art. 32 of the Federal Constitution.
78745.m: Because of the presumption of innocence, everyone counts as innocent until proven guilty.

78746.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78746.e: The hourglass and the calendar show that a lot of time passes until the claim disappears. After a certain period, a claim or an offence can no longer be pursued; this is called the statute of limitations.
78746.m: Once the limitation period has passed, a claim can no longer be enforced.

78747.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
a: Right to exclude others from your home
78747.e: Folders with information about a person are protected by a lock and a shield. Data protection rules how personal data may be handled; in Switzerland the revised Data Protection Act has applied since 2023.
78747.m: Data protection protects people from misuse of their personal data.

78748.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78748.e: Someone is not happy with a verdict (thumbs down) and goes to the next higher court. This legal remedy is called an appeal.
78748.m: With an appeal, you have a higher court review a verdict.

78749.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78749.e: The 18th birthday, the signature and the scales show that from the age of 18 you may sign contracts yourself. In Switzerland the age of majority has been 18 since 1996.
78749.m: Once you come of age, you may sign contracts on your own.

78750.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78750.e: A speaking head, a speech bubble, an open lock and scales stand for the right to express your opinion freely. Freedom of expression is guaranteed in Art. 16 of the Federal Constitution.
78750.m: Freedom of expression allows you to say your opinion openly.

78751.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78751.e: After an accident the car is repaired and the loss is made good with money, as the court decides. Anyone who unlawfully causes damage to another person must pay damages (Art. 41 of the Code of Obligations).
78751.m: Anyone who unlawfully causes damage to someone must pay damages.

78752.q: Which philosophical term do these pictures stand for?
78752.e: The zero in front of the universe and the shrug mean that nothing has a fixed meaning or value. This attitude is called nihilism (Latin nihil, nothing); Friedrich Nietzsche dealt with it intensively.
78752.m: Nihilism denies that there are fixed values or a meaning.

78753.q: Which philosophical term do these pictures stand for?
78753.e: Gold, a rule book, a handshake and the double arrow stand for a rule that works in both directions. The Golden Rule roughly says: treat others as you want to be treated yourself.
78753.m: The Golden Rule asks you to treat others as you would like to be treated.

78754.q: Which saying of an ancient philosopher do these pictures stand for?
a: “Man is the measure of all things”
78754.e: A bearded thinker points to his brain, shrugs and holds up a zero. The saying is attributed to Socrates and expresses that recognising your own ignorance is the beginning of wisdom.
78754.m: Socrates saw knowing your own ignorance as the beginning of wisdom.

78755.q: Which philosophical term do these pictures stand for?
78755.e: Eyes, ears, nose and hand lead to the brain: knowledge comes from sense experience. This teaching is called empiricism; an important representative was John Locke.
78755.m: Empiricism sees sense experience as the source of all knowledge.

78756.q: Which philosophical term do these pictures stand for?
78756.e: A body, the sign for two and a mind show that a human being consists of two substances. René Descartes held this mind-body dualism.
78756.m: Dualism distinguishes between body and mind as two separate substances.

78757.q: Which philosophical term do these pictures stand for?
78757.e: Many happy faces, a plus and numbers stand for the greatest happiness of the greatest number. According to the utilitarianism of Jeremy Bentham and John Stuart Mill, the good action is the one that maximises overall benefit.
78757.m: Utilitarianism judges actions by their benefit for as many people as possible.

78758.q: Which philosophical paradox do these pictures stand for?
78758.e: A runner, a tortoise, a finishing line and the infinity sign point to Zeno of Elea: swift Achilles seems never to catch the tortoise, because he would have to cover infinitely many stretches.
78758.m: Zeno’s paradox of Achilles and the tortoise plays with infinitely many stretches.

78759.q: Which philosophical thought experiment do these pictures stand for?
78759.e: All the wooden parts of a ship are replaced one by one, and the question is whether it is still the same ship. Plutarch passed down this thought experiment about identity.
78759.m: The Ship of Theseus asks whether something is still the same after all its parts are replaced.

78760.q: Which psychology term do these pictures stand for?
78760.e: Several groups point at a single, stressed person. Peer pressure arises when someone feels pushed to adapt to a group’s behaviour.
78760.m: Peer pressure can make people act against their own opinion.

78762.q: Which psychology term do these pictures stand for?
78762.e: A climber is completely relaxed and absorbed in what she is doing, time flies and everything flows like a wave. Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi called this state of complete absorption flow.
78762.m: In flow you are so absorbed that you forget the time.

78763.q: Which psychology term do these pictures stand for?
78763.e: A briefcase, a flame, a candle and an exhausted face show that someone is burnt out inside from work. This state of deep exhaustion is called burnout.
78763.m: Burnout is a state of deep exhaustion from long overload.

78764.q: Which term from psychology do these pictures mean?
78764.e: Sun and a thought bubble with a sleepy face make day and dream. In a daydream, your thoughts wander while you are awake.
78764.m: In a daydream, your thoughts wander even though you are awake.

78765.q: Which psychology term do these pictures stand for?
78765.e: A house, a broken heart and a suitcase show someone far away who misses their home. This feeling is called homesickness; it was once considered a typical “Swiss illness”.
78765.m: Homesickness is longing for home when you are far away.

78766.q: Which psychology term do these pictures stand for?
78766.e: A brain, a stopwatch and a note flying away show that information is kept only briefly. According to George A. Miller, short-term memory stores about seven items for a short time.
78766.m: Short-term memory keeps only a little information for a short time.

78767.q: Which psychology term do these pictures stand for?
78767.e: A person reads quietly alone at home with the sound switched off. Introversion describes people who tend to recharge their energy in peace and alone; the term goes back to Carl Gustav Jung.
78767.m: Introverted people tend to recharge their energy in peace and alone.

78768.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78768.e: A plant, a caterpillar, a bird and an eagle stand in a row in which each living thing is eaten by the next. Such a linear sequence of feeding relationships is called a food chain.
78768.m: In a food chain, each link is food for the next.

78769.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78769.e: A butterfly, frog, mushroom, ladybird, hedgehog and plant show many different living things. The variety of species, genes and habitats is called biodiversity.
78769.m: Biodiversity means the variety of life on Earth.

78770.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78770.e: Only maize grows on the whole field, one plant next to the other. Growing a single crop over a large area is called monoculture.
78770.m: In a monoculture only one single plant species is grown on an area.

78771.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78771.e: A banana skin and carrots are broken down by worms, and a new plant grows from them. In composting, small creatures break down plant remains into nutrient-rich soil.
78771.m: Composting turns plant remains into fertile soil.

78772.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78772.e: A bee carries pollen from one flower to the next. This transfer of pollen is called pollination and is needed so that many plants can form fruit.
78772.m: In pollination, pollen reaches the stigma of a flower.

78773.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78773.e: A lamp lights up the city at night so brightly that you can no longer see the stars and nocturnal animals like the owl are disturbed. This brightening of the night sky by artificial light is called light pollution.
78773.m: Light pollution disturbs nocturnal animals and hides the starry sky.

78774.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78774.e: Factory fumes form clouds from which rain falls that damages trees. Sulphur and nitrogen oxides make the rain acidic; in the 1980s this was part of the debate about “dying forests”.
78774.m: Acid rain forms when exhaust gases combine with water in the air to make acids.

78775.q: Which ecology term do these pictures stand for?
78775.e: A fishing boat with a net catches so many fish that their numbers fall. When more fish are caught than can grow back, it is called overfishing.
78775.m: Overfishing means more fish are caught than can grow back.

78776.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78776.e: Lots of emails that go straight into the bin stand for unwanted mass messages. Such messages are called spam.
78776.m: Spam is unwanted mass email that usually ends up in the bin.

78777.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78777.e: A key (password) plus a mobile phone with a number code lead to access. With two-factor authentication you need two independent proofs to log in.
78777.m: Two-factor authentication protects accounts with a second proof.

78778.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures mean?
78778.e: A screen (mobile and computer) is photographed. A photo of the screen is called a screenshot.
78778.m: With a screenshot, you save a picture of the screen.

78779.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78779.e: A person takes a selfie, lots of people follow them, and their reach grows. Someone who has many followers on social media and influences their opinions or shopping habits is called an influencer.
78779.m: Influencers use their reach on social media to influence many people.

78780.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78780.e: A film plays over the internet straight away, like a flowing stream. With streaming, video or music is transmitted and played at the same time, without being fully downloaded first.
78780.m: With streaming, a film plays while it is still being transmitted.

78781.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78781.e: A robot with a brain has an idea. Computer systems that solve tasks which would otherwise need human intelligence are called artificial intelligence (AI).
78781.m: Artificial intelligence lets computers solve tasks that require thinking.

78782.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78782.e: A headset, a globe and a game controller stand for diving into a computer-generated world. With a VR headset you experience virtual reality.
78782.m: With a VR headset you dive into a virtual reality.

78783.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78783.e: A crossed-out mobile phone, a tree and a person meditating show a deliberate break from digital devices. This time out is called a digital detox.
78783.m: In a digital detox you deliberately do without digital devices for a while.

78784.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures stand for?
78784.e: A floppy disk and two identical folders show that files are copied and saved. Such a safety copy is called a backup.
78784.m: A backup is a safety copy that protects against data loss.

78785.q: Which linguistics term do these pictures stand for?
78785.e: Two different words (A and B) point to the same thing, such as bike and bicycle. Words with the same or a very similar meaning are called synonyms.
78785.m: Synonyms are different words with the same or a similar meaning.

78786.q: Which linguistics term do these pictures stand for?
78786.e: Mountains, a speaking head and a village stand for a form of language tied to a region. Such a regional variety of a language is called a dialect, for example Bernese German or Valais German.
78786.m: A dialect is a regional form of a language.

78788.q: Which linguistics term do these pictures stand for?
78788.e: A word comes in from the wider world and becomes at home in your own language. A loanword is taken from another language and adapted, for example the German word “Fenster” (window) from Latin fenestra.
78788.m: A loanword comes from another language but feels native.

78789.q: Which linguistics term do these pictures stand for?
78789.e: The sign for new, letters and a speech bubble show a newly created word. Newly created words such as “to google” are called neologisms.
78789.m: A neologism is a newly created word.

78790.q: Which term from linguistics do these pictures mean?
78790.e: Hands and hand signs replace the spoken word. Deaf people communicate with sign language; in Switzerland there are three sign languages.
78790.m: Sign languages are full languages that work with the hands, the face and the body.

78791.q: Which linguistics term do these pictures stand for?
78791.e: A word, a family tree, a clock and a magnifying glass show that the origin and history of a word are being studied. This discipline is called etymology.
78791.m: Etymology studies the origin and history of words.

78792.q: Which linguistics term do these pictures stand for?
78792.e: A mouth, a loudspeaker and a microscope show that speech sounds are studied closely. The science of how sounds are produced and perceived is called phonetics.
78792.m: Phonetics studies how speech sounds are made and heard.

78793.q: Which invention do these pictures stand for?
78793.e: A device that lets you see the moon enlarged from far away. A patent for the telescope was applied for in the Netherlands in 1608; Galileo Galilei pointed it at the sky in 1609.
78793.m: From the 17th century, the telescope let people observe distant celestial bodies.

78794.q: Which invention do these pictures stand for?
78794.e: Fire heats air, which lifts a balloon into the clouds. In 1783 the Montgolfier brothers launched the first crewed hot-air balloon in France.
78794.m: A hot-air balloon rises because warm air is lighter than cold air.

78795.q: Which invention do these pictures stand for?
78795.e: A cow, a syringe and a protective shield: in 1796 Edward Jenner transferred harmless cowpox to protect against dangerous smallpox. The word vaccine comes from Latin vacca, cow.
78795.m: Edward Jenner’s smallpox vaccination was the first scientific vaccination.

78796.q: Which invention do these pictures stand for?
78796.e: Light and writing make a picture: photography means “drawing with light” in Greek. Joseph Nicéphore Niépce made the oldest surviving photograph around 1826.
78796.m: The word photography means “drawing with light”.

78797.q: Which invention do these pictures stand for?
